Sunderland agree £25.6m fee for defender Methalie
- Published
Sunderland have agreed a £25.6m fee to sign left-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.
The 20-year-old French defender is expected to undergo a medical after a verbal agreement was reached for an initial £23.9m, with a further £1.7m in potential add-ons.
Methalie made 28 appearances for Toulouse in Ligue 1 last season, scoring twice in his final three games, as they finished ninth.
The deal follows a prolonged pursuit by Regis Le Bris' side as Sunderland look to strengthen their defence before the start of their Premier League campaign at Ipswich Town next Saturday (15:00 BST).
The Black Cats will also compete in Europe for the first time in 53 years and are looking to add greater depth to their squad.
Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who signed on a free transfer from Lille, remains the only completed transfer so far in the window for Sunderland.

Diagnostics startup Redcliffe Labs has partnered with spacetech startup Skyroot Aerospace to test the stability and performance of diagnostic reagents in space. As part of the collaboration’s first experiment, dubbed DRIFT-1, Redcliffe’s dry diagnostic reagents will be placed in Low Earth Orbit for 90 days. Their performance will subsequently be compared with that of an identical control sample maintained on Earth. The startups said in a statement that the experiment would examine how exposure to the space environment affects the reagents’ stability and performance. The initiative is also expected to generate flight data that could support the development of diagnostic technologies for space missions and challenging environments on Earth. However, the statement did not disclose the proposed launch timeline, the rocket or spacecraft that would carry the reagents, the number and types of reagents involved, or the financial terms of the partnership. Redcliffe said the findings could help it develop diagnostic products for locations where access to conventional laboratory infrastructure or cold-chain facilities is limited. The two startups are also exploring potential applications across astronaut healthcare, life sciences, microgravity research, and point-of-care diagnostics for human spaceflight programmes, including Gaganyaan and the proposed Bharatiya Antariksh Station. “If we can build diagnostics that withstand the rigours of space, we can create more resilient technologies that improve access to reliable healthcare in some of the most challenging environments on Earth,” Redcliffe founder and CEO Aditya Kandoi said. Founded in 2018 by Kandoi, Dheeraj Jain, and Ashish Dubey, Redcliffe offers pathology and diagnostic services through its laboratories, collection centres, and home sample collection network. It claims to operate across more than 220 cities and offer over 3,600 diagnostic tests. The healthtech startup has raised around $115 Mn in funding to date. In September 2024, it raised $42 Mn in a Series C round led by Denmark’s Investment Fund for Developing Countries, with participation from LeapFrog Investments, HealthQuad, and Spark Growth Ventures. Redcliffe has also been expanding its diagnostics network through acquisitions. Inc42 exclusively reported last month that it was in talks to acquire Pune-based Megavision Diagnostics Center, adding two MRI-equipped centres to its network. The acquisition was completed this month. This followed its acquisitions of diagnostic centres in Ajmer and Kota. In April, Redcliffe divested its fertility services business, Crysta IVF, to sharpen its focus on diagnostics. The development comes less than a month after Skyroot’s Vikram-I undertook the first orbital rocket launch by an Indian private company from the country. The rocket lifted off from ISRO’s Satish Dhawan Space Centre on July 18 and deployed two satellites into Low Earth Orbit. Founded in 2018 by Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Hyderabad-based Skyroot develops small-satellite launch vehicles under its Vikram series. The spacetech unicorn has raised more than $95 Mn in funding to date from investors such as Temasek, GIC, and Sherpalo Ventures.

Canadian women clinch berth in LA 2028 with semifinal win at flag football world championships
Canadian women defeat world No. 1 Mexico 20-6 in semifinal
The Canadian women's flag football team is bound for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.
Canada defeated Mexico 20-6 in an International Federation of American Football (IFAF) world championship semifinal Saturday in Duesseldorf, Germany.
"I am so proud of this team," said Canadian women's team head coach Rachel Lessard in a statement. "Qualifying for the 2028 Olympic Games is a reflection of the discipline, resilience and trust this team has built over the course of this process, and they've earned every bit of this opportunity at the 2026 IFAF Flag Football world championships.
"Canadian flag football is on the rise, and we're honoured to officially be able to help carry that momentum to the 2028 Olympic Games."
The top two countries in each of the men's and women's world championships qualified for 2028 when flag football makes its Olympic debut.
But if the United States, already qualified as host, reached either final, the top three finishers qualified for L.A.
The Canadian women will meet the U.S., which was a 27-21 semifinal winner over Britain, for the world title Sunday.
Mexico and Britain will battle for the remaining women's Olympic berth in the bronze-medal game.
Canada's men fell 41-36 to Italy in Saturday's semifinal, but still had a chance to punch an early Olympic ticket in Sunday's bronze-medal match against Mexico.
The U.S. was a 42-40 winner over the Mexicans in the other semifinal, and faces Italy for men's gold Sunday at the world championship.
Countries can also qualify for Los Angeles via next year's continental championships and a qualifying series the following year.
The Canadian men defeated American Samoa 24-14 and the women were 40-12 victors over Austria in Saturday's quarterfinals.
Canada's women edged the U.S. 34-33 at the USA Football Summer Series on June 19.
"This is an incredible moment for our women's flag football team and everyone who has supported them along the way," said Eva Havaris, Football Canada's chief executive officer. "This group worked incredibly hard for this moment, delivered an outstanding performance and it goes without saying that they've earned it.
"We're thrilled to see them officially secure their place on the Olympic stage, and we can't wait to see what they do in Los Angeles."
Sara Parker passed for 107 yards in Saturday's semifinal. Silvia Contreras led Canada's receivers with 38 yards on six catches, and also scored a touchdown.
Caroline Moquin-Joubert scored a pair of touchdowns and Alexane Fournier also reached the end zone.
James Drysdale compiled 76 yards on six catches and also scored a touchdown for Canada's men in the semifinal loss. Jackson Tachinski and Antony Auclair also scored.

Ever since I began ranking Ina Garten's pasta dishes back in 2021, nothing has come close to topping her weeknight Bolognese.
That all changed when I tried her penne alla vodka.
The recipe was inspired by one of Garten's favorite dishes, the Penne Alla Vecchia Bettola from Nick & Toni's, a restaurant in East Hampton.
Now, it has a permanent spot on my list of best Barefoot Contessa dishes.
You probably already have most of the ingredients for Ina Garten's penne alla vodka.
To make Garten's penne alla vodka for four, you'll need:
- ¾ pound of penne (Garten recommends DeCecco)
- 2 ½ cups of chopped yellow onions
- 2 28-ounce cans of whole peeled plum tomatoes, drained
- 3 minced garlic cloves
- 1 cup of vodka
- 1 cup of heavy cream
- ½ cup of freshly grated Parmesan cheese (plus extra for serving)
- ¼ cup of good olive oil
- 2 tablespoons of chopped fresh oregano leaves (plus extra for serving)
- 1 ½ teaspoons of dried oregano
- ½ teaspoon of red pepper flakes
To get started, I chopped my onions and minced my garlic.
My prep was done in a matter of minutes.
I threw the onions into my Dutch oven, where I had already heated some olive oil.
I cooked my onions over medium-low heat for about five minutes, until they turned translucent.
I added the garlic, red pepper flakes, and oregano once my onions were cooked.
I cooked everything together for one minute.
Then I added the vodka.
The recipe says to simmer everything together for about five to seven minutes, until the mixture has reduced by half.
Next, I threw in the whole peeled plum tomatoes.
I crushed each whole tomato into the pot with my hand, per Garten's instructions.
After seasoning the sauce with salt and pepper, I covered my pot and threw it into the oven.
The sauce needs to bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes, so I started cooking long before dinner.
It's not the quickest meal, but I promise this dish is worth the wait!
Just before my sauce was ready, I began cooking the pasta.
I brought a large pot of salted water to a boil and added the penne.
I cooked my pasta until it was al dente, which took about 10 minutes. Then I drained my noodles and set them aside.
Once my sauce was out of the oven, I threw it in the blender.
Garten says to purée the tomato mixture using a blender or food processor until it's smooth.
I poured my puréed tomato mixture back into the Dutch oven.
I seasoned the mixture with salt and pepper, then added the fresh oregano and heavy cream.
The color transformed as I stirred the pot.
The hue reminded me of the famous vodka pasta at Jon & Vinny's in Los Angeles.
I partially covered my Dutch oven and let the sauce simmer.
The sauce should simmer for 10 minutes.
When my sauce was ready, I threw in the pasta.
I let the pasta cook for two more minutes in the sauce.
I took my Dutch oven off the heat and stirred in the Parmesan cheese.
Dinner was ready!
As I topped everything with extra Parmesan and oregano, I couldn't help but admire the dish.
This is, without a doubt, the most beautiful pasta I've ever made.
Garten's penne alla vodka is simply fantastic.
The sauce is so creamy and smooth without being heavy and overwhelming. Slowly roasting the tomato sauce in the oven added depth and complexity to the vodka sauce, which I actually loved even more than my favorite from Jon & Vinny's. My only wish was that I had made some of Garten's "outrageous" garlic bread to go with it!
While Garten's pasta needs a bit more time in the oven, it doesn't require many steps. The actual prep and cooking were pretty minimal, but the penne still looked really impressive.
Whether you need a recipe to dazzle everyone with or want to whip up a comforting dish, there's truly no better pasta than this.

- The claim that sailors and Marines aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier are facing deteriorating conditions after nearly 260 days at sea is still under investigation. It stemmed from an MS NOW report published on Aug. 5, 2026.
- MS NOW says the sailors are running out of food and other essential supplies, such as soap and toothpaste. The article also says there are safety concerns and the crew's morale is low. The news media outlet quoted Cmdr. Joseph Hontz, the spokesperson for the Navy's 5th Fleet, as saying the crew is "resilient."
- In April 2026, U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth deemed previous reports of food shortages on the USS Abraham Lincoln to be "fake news" in an X post.
- Snopes will update this report if additional information surfaces. We have reached out to the U.S. Navy, the 5th Fleet and the Department of the Defense and are waiting for responses. We also contacted the office of Sen. Cory Booker, a Democrat from New Jersey, who amplified the claim.
A rumor spread online in August 2026 that sailors and Marines on the U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, deployed in the Arabian Sea as of this writing, are facing food and supply shortages, mold and other deteriorating conditions.
The claim spread on X and Facebook as the U.S. war against Iran entered its sixth month. Sen. Cory Booker, a Democrat from New Jersey, amplified the alleged story in an X post, saying (archived), in part, "We cannot claim to support the troops while leaving them hungry. Our service members deserve better."
Booker's post includes a video by @pullupspastapolitics, a woman who refers to herself as an "independent reporter" and makes content on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram.
In the clip, the woman quoted from an MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) report published on Aug. 5 (archived). She said families of those on the ship "are upset and they're blaming" U.S. President Donald Trump.
MS NOW's report says that sailors and Marines are lacking basic necessities and families are speaking out:
Moldy showers. Food shortages. Sailors running out of toothpaste, deodorant and soap.
Families of the sailors and Marines aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are sounding the alarm that their loved ones are so exhausted they fear it could lead to deadly mistakes, as the carrier enters its ninth month at sea and its fifth consecutive month of combat operations against Iran.
The report then says the families are concerned that the low morale and safety conditions are making the deployment very risky as the Trump administration continues its military campaign against Iran. The article also quotes Cmdr. Joseph Hontz, the spokesperson for the Navy's 5th Fleet, as saying the crew is "resilient."
It was not possible to directly obtain confirmation of the reportedly dire conditions on the ship. For this reason, we left this claim unrated.
Snopes contacted the U.S. Navy, the 5th Fleet and the Department of Defense seeking details. We also reached out to Booker's office, asking if he had received direct reports from crew members or their families. We will update this report should any of them respond.
It is true that the USS Abraham Lincoln has been at sea for 259 days as of this writing, according to Cruising Earth, a website that tracks ships. It reportedly left its homeport of San Diego on Nov. 21, 2025, for routine operations and was then deployed to the Arabian Sea after the war on Iran began.
This is not the first time families have reported food shortages on the same ship since its deployment. In April 2026, some news outlets reported concerns that the roughly 5,000-member crew was surviving on little food. At the time, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth took to X (archived) to dismiss this as "FAKE NEWS."
For further reading, Snopes previously investigated photographs that accompanied these reports in April 2026.

West Ham break EFL record to sign Engels for £22m
- Published
West Ham United have broken the EFL transfer record by paying a £22m fee to sign midfielder Arne Engels from Scottish champions Celtic.
The 22-year-old Belgium international has signed a five-year contract after West Ham paid what they called a "record fee paid by an EFL Championship club".
It tops the £17.5m paid by Ipswich Town a year ago to sign Norway forward Sindre Walle Egeli.
Following relegation in May, West Ham start their first Championship season since 2012 with a trip to Burnley on Sunday.
But Engels, who scored 17 goals and provided 22 assists in 100 Celtic appearances, will not be available to make his debut until the home league derby against Charlton Athletic at the London Stadium on Saturday, 22 August.
Engels is West Ham's fourth summer signing after the recruitment of Venezuela midfielder Keiber Lamadrid, Dutch defender Joel Veltman and Israel winger Manor Solomon.
West Ham director of player recruitment Nils Koppen told the club website:, external "Arne is a player we have been tracking for some time as a key target.
"For a player who is still very young with his best years in front of him, he has very good experience and has established himself at a big club, showing consistency and confidence.
"Arne has the right traits, both as a player and as a character, to fit into what we are trying to build moving forward. He is very motivated to be here for this challenge."
Engels, who has made four appearances for Belgium, won back-to-back Scottish Premiership titles with Celtic after arriving from Augsburg in August 2024, having begun his career at Club Brugge.
"It's a really nice project to come into," he said. "To try to go back to the Premier League. That's the big goal.
"It's just up to me to hopefully help the team with it and together with the supporters to get some wins. Hopefully it's going to be a good year."

The Canadian airline WestJet has agreed to pay C$4.5m (£2.4m) to settle a decade-long sexual harassment class action lawsuit levelled by its female flight attendants, who alleged the company failed to maintain a safe workplace.
The suit followed allegations by Mandalena Lewis, a former flight attendant, that a pilot had sexually assaulted her and a colleague, but that WestJet kept the pilot flying, thereby putting other employees at risk.
A British Columbia judge on Monday approved the terms of the settlement, which were finalised on 22 June after months of negotiation. The payment will be distributed among the 3,452 flight attendants in the class action after expenses are removed, including legal fees.
WestJet agreed to hire a third-party to conduct a workplace inquiry that will examine the prevalence of harassment, the extent of underreporting and how reporting systems can be made more effective.
The suit had called on WestJet to implement mandatory anti-harassment training for pilots, along with an admission of wrongdoing and an admission of a breach of employee contract. None were included in the settlement.
Lewis filed the initial class action against the airline in April 2016. She said she was dismayed by the results, especially given that two years ago WestJet paid out $12.5m in a baggage fee class action, nearly three times the amount agreed to in the sexual harassment suit.
“I’m glad it’s over … but I’m just exhausted. I’m shaking my head,” she said, adding that she was advised the amount was the most that could be achieved given that legal expenses were piling up.
Under BC law, the suit included all female flight attendants who worked for the company between 4 April 2014 and 28 February 2021, because Lewis’s suit alleged that all of them had their contracts violated by WestJet during that period because its employee policy promised that the workplace would be free from harassment.
The suit claimed WestJet broke its policy by not taking enough steps to address reports of assault or to prevent harassment in the first place.
Lewis said she was sexually assaulted by a WestJet pilot while on a layover in Hawaii in 2010 when she was 25 years old. In court documents, she said the same pilot had also assaulted another flight attendant in 2008.
Though she reported the assault to WestJet, the pilot remained at the company and Lewis was eventually fired in 2016 for “gross insubordination”, according to court documents submitted by WestJet that year, which she and her legal team allege was retaliation for trying to hold the airline accountable internally.
She said she abandoned an individual civil claim and instead created the class action after learning other flight attendants had also experienced harassment.
Lewis said she reported the assault to police in Maui but alleges WestJet rerouted the pilot so he would not face questioning in Hawaii.
She said fellow members of the class action suit were also disappointed with the result. Eight of them had already asked the province’s supreme court not to approve the settlement in February when some of the details first emerged, citing a low payout and a lack of accountability by WestJet.
“We didn’t get justice here,” said Lewis.
The case garnered national attention for exposing pilot behaviour toward female flight attendants and the vulnerability of the scores of young women who have historically been the target demographic for the job.
A 2018 survey of more than 3,500 flight attendants by the US Association of Flight Attendants found that 68% had experienced sexual harassment in their careers while only 7% had reported an incident to their employer.
WestJet did not respond to questions about Lewis’s claims of assault, and the allegations that it failed to keep the workplace free of harassment and does not properly investigate alleged sexual assaults.
In a statement, the company said it was “pleased to have reached a mutually agreed upon settlement”. It said: “We are committed to strengthening our operations and training, focused on the safety and wellbeing of all WestJetters and we are focused on advancing a culture of empowerment.”

UN rights experts have urged Canada to take all feasible measures to protect the Sikh activist Moninder Singh, who has been repeatedly warned by the Canadian authorities of credible threats to his life.
In a letter to the Canadian government, the five UN experts raised “concerning allegations of foreign intimidation and reprisals” against Singh, a Canadian national.
The letter recalled that since 2022, Singh has received four “duty to warn” notices from the Canadian authorities about credible and imminent threats to his life. It urged Canada to “take all feasible measures at its disposal to protect Mr Moninder Singh and his family, as well as similarly situated individuals on Canadian soil”.
It went on to say: “We also urge the authorities to accelerate the investigations into these allegations, hold perpetrators accountable, ensure adequate remedy to victims and take all steps to prevent reoccurrence.”
The letter, dated 3 June and made public two months later, was written by the special rapporteurs on: protecting rights while countering terrorism; freedom of peaceful assembly; human rights defenders; freedom of religion; and the expert on promoting a democratic international order.
UN special rapporteurs and experts are independent figures appointed by the Human Rights Council to report their findings. They do not, therefore, speak for the UN itself. A copy of the letter was also sent to the Indian government.
Singh visited the UN in Geneva earlier this year to appeal for international action against India’s alleged targeting of Sikh activists abroad and against transnational repression more broadly. Sikh activists accuse India of targeting members of their community around the world, including alleged killings using organised crime groups – charges that India denies.
The best-known case was the 2023 killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a friend of Singh’s who was shot dead near the Sikh temple he led in a Vancouver suburb. Canada’s then-prime minister, Justin Trudeau, publicly accused India of involvement in that assassination, a charge later repeated by Canadian intelligence.
India denied the allegations but the row chilled ties between the two nations, both of which expelled a string of diplomats in 2024.
Relations improved after the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, took office last year, culminating with an India visit in March to sign a string of trade deals, as Canadian authorities downplayed their previous threat assessment.
Like Nijjar, Singh, 44, is part of a fringe group advocating for an independent Sikh state called Khalistan. The Khalistan campaign dates to India’s 1947 independence and has been blamed for the assassination of a prime minister and the bombing of a passenger jet. It has been a contentious issue between India and several western nations with large Sikh populations.
In their letter, the experts said they were concerned that the threats against Singh “fall within a broader pattern of transnational repression by Indian authorities against Sikh activists in different countries, including Canada”.
Singh said the letter was “a stark reminder of how far the Indian state is willing to go to silence Sikh voices advocating for self-determination”.
“When a foreign state feels empowered to commit violence in Canada to silence dissent, it signals a profound failure to protect the rights and safety of targeted communities,” he said.
“I refuse to be intimidated into silence. My leadership and advocacy for Khalistan are rooted in international law, human rights principles and most importantly the lived experiences of my community,” Singh added.

The Food and Drug Administration on Thursday approved an oral treatment for advanced multiple myeloma made by Bristol Myers Squibb, marking the debut of a new class of medicine for the blood cancer and the first drug cleared by U.S. regulators using a more sensitive measure of remission.
The Bristol drug, iberdomide, will be sold under the brand name Zenbexus. It will be used in combination with two other drugs, Darzalex and dexamethasone, to treat patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy.
“With the Zenbexus approval, Bristol is the first company to bring a novel class of drugs to patients with multiple myeloma, opening venues for many more potential combinations,” said Cristian Massacesi, Bristol’s chief medical officer, in an interview with STAT ahead of the approval announcement.

Topline
An Iranian embassy pushed the social media conspiracy that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt resigned from her job this week because President Donald Trump left her on the plane he evacuated in Turkey to evade an alleged threat from Iran—but it’s unlikely she was actually on the so-called decoy flight.
Key Facts
The embassy of Iran in South Africa posted a photo of Leavitt on X Saturday and commended her resignation, writing, "betrayal is awful. When your boss betrays you and sends you in danger, while he escapes in a food truck, you lose all hope for camaraderie. Of course, you can’t expect much more from a murderer.”
Social media conspiracists speculated this week that Leavitt resigned over the incident—when Trump hid in a catering truck to be moved off Air Force One and onto another plane while departing Turkey last month to evade an alleged threat from Iran, according to multiple reports.
The White House disputed the rumor, telling the fact-checking website Snopes, “this is not true, she was not on the trip.”
New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman, who reported on the ruse, also told Snopes neither she nor Leavitt were on the flight.
Leavitt gave birth to her second child May 1 and returned to the White House podium on July 16, though she was back at work several weeks earlier, posting a photo of herself aboard the new Air Force One jet gifted from Qatar on July 1, when it made its inaugural flight to South Dakota.
Leavitt announced on Wednesday she was resigning from her role to spend more time with her family, writing that since returning from maternity leave, she feels she “cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary.”
Tangent
Leavitt, who is expected to leave her job at the end of the month, called her decision “bittersweet” and said she will “always remain a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party.” Trump said he understood and respected Leavitt’s decision in a Truth Social post, adding that she will be one of his “top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party.”
Key Background
Trump was secretly shuttled off an Air Force One jet and taken to a smaller, Air Force Boeing C-32A plane via a catering truck just before departing Ankara, Turkey, on July 8 multiple outlets reported. Trump initially said he would take the older Air Force One plane, instead of the newly outfitted jet from Qatar that he flew to Turkey on, “for old time’s sake.” He took a select few aides with him, including Natalie Harp and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, but left two cabinet members, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, along with other aides and journalists on the trip to Turkey, on the so-called decoy flight, the New York Times reported. The operation happened after U.S. intelligence officials determined a credible threat against the president involving Iran, according to multiple outlets. The legitimacy of the threat, reportedly initiated by Israeli intelligence, has been widely disputed, including by some CIA officials, according to multiple outlets. Iranian state media and Iran’s embassy in South Africa mocked the ruse, posting memes of Trump pictured inside of catering carts full of food.

Many Canadians are boycotting the US, so this is where they're travelling instead
- Published
Prior to US President Donald Trump's re-election, Kent Truscott and his family, from London, Ontario, had taken multiple trips south of the border, including to California and most recently New York in 2023.
But since late 2024, "my family and I have completely decided to boycott the United States", he told BBC.
That meant cancelling a trip last spring to Texas to watch the SpaceX Starship launch with his brother. The two had planned to fly down from Toronto, rent a car and stay a week to watch the launch, likely spending "thousands of dollars".
Truscott and his wife decided to spend that money in Canada instead – the Atlantic provinces of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island, to be exact.
Their decision is a response to US tariffs and the president's comments about annexing their country. More than a year after Trump's return to the White House, many Canadians like Truscott are still holding firm on their boycott on travel to the US.
Even with a slight uptick in road trips to the US in April, Canadians made 800,000 fewer trips that month compared to the same time in 2024, before Trump was elected, according to national data.
The boycott has meant a loss of about C$3.3bn ($2.35bn; £1.75bn) in travel revenue for the US last year - money that Canadians have instead chosen to spend overseas or exploring their own country.
That financial void has been felt by a number of American cities and states, who have urged Canadians to return through targeted advertisements and special deals. In July, New York City's tourism board said it will offer Broadway tickets and hotel rooms to Canadian tourists at a 30% discount.
The BBC spoke to a few Canadians about why they have chosen to avoid the US, where they have gone instead and what it would take for them to return.
Not everyone is driven solely by Trump's treatment of Canada, with some noting that the declining Canadian dollar has also made the US less affordable.
But many say they feel their country's relationship with the US has hit a breaking point, and that it would take a lot for them to return, if at all.
Trading Texas for Atlantic Canada
Once they decided to vacation in Atlantic Canada, Kent Truscott and his wife embraced the idea of discovering their own country. They rented a vehicle, hiked the scenic Cabot Trail and stayed at a resort on the Atlantic Ocean run entirely by women.
"I had the best halibut dinner in my life, caught by someone that morning out on the bay," he recalled.
He added that he was unsure when he would return to the US again. "There has been a fundamental break," Truscott said, noting anti-immigration raids and other Trump policies that he does not agree with, as well as the president's rhetoric and actions against Canada.
"As much as I would like to say that when Donald Trump leaves everything will go back to normal, well, 70 million people voted for it," he said.
A cancelled cruise through the Panama canal
Lynda Rousseau and her husband Joe had lived in Texas for 19 years prior to retiring in their home country of Canada. Their move back was scheduled for last summer, but was pushed earlier to February 2025 because of their anger over Trump's re-election.
"We just couldn't stand the idea of living there while he was running things," Rousseau, who now lives in Ottawa, said.
She and her husband then decided to boycott the US altogether after Trump began calling Canada "the 51st state" and its former prime minister, Justin Trudeau, "governor".
That summer, the couple cancelled a cruise that was due to depart from New York City and go through the Panama canal. Instead, they rebooked with the same company on a different cruise through Rome and Barcelona, where Rousseau said they enjoyed exploring ancient ruins and eating delicious food.
"I mean it's not New York's fault... but Trump is in charge of it all, and so it all takes a hit," Rousseau said.
The couple, who are dual US and Canada citizens, had also scrapped their plans of becoming "snowbirds" – a term used to describe Canadians who spend the cold winter months in warm US states like Florida and Arizona.
They now only cross the border occasionally to pick up their mail and come back, Rousseau said, avoiding spending any money while there.
Rousseau added that she mourns the loss of convenience of being able to drive and spend time in the US, which can be much cheaper to visit than most overseas destinations due to sheer proximity.
But through the boycott, she said she gained "a little more pride in Canada".
City hopping in Morocco in lieu of California
Nick Smith was never a Trump fan. The Vancouver retiree had stopped going on road trips to Seattle and to major US national parks with his children after the president was first elected in 2016.
He said he resumed his trips south of the border when Joe Biden took over, but is now back to avoiding the US, especially after seeing many of his fellow Canadians boycott as well.
"Now we're just not even considering it," he said.
Smith has even avoided taking connecting flights through American cities to other destinations. Last autumn, he and his friends travelled to Mexico City and opted for a direct flight from Vancouver instead.
Earlier this year, he and his wife Sylvia travelled to Morocco for the first time, stopping through cities like Marrakech, Fez and Essaouira. One of their favourite moments, he said, is experiencing the Muslim country during the month of Ramadan.
"It was actually quite an interesting time to be there, and realising how important religion is to the people of Morocco and how seriously they take the fasting ritual," Smith said. "We just don't have anything like that in Canada."
Asked if he would return to the US if Trump leaves the White House, Smith said: "It certainly is going to have to be more than that."
"I would need to see some sense of reconciliation [with Canada]... actions that would show a return back to amicable relations," he said.
A bucket list hike finally fulfilled
Christie Mitchell has made countless trips to the US in her lifetime. She has hiked national parks, attended American football games and drove an RV through several states down to Florida.
The 50-year-old mother of two from the town of Powell River, British Columbia, even remembers a time when you didn't need a passport to cross the border.
"I'm of that generation where I thought [Canada and the US] were just one big country," she said. "I just always felt welcome."
But that feeling has faded under the current administration, she said, which she does not want to support with her purchasing power.
"It breaks my heart, because I love Americans and I love America."
Boycotting travel to the US pushed Mitchell towards accomplishing a goal she has always had: hiking the 490-mile (790km) Camino Francés route through Spain.
She did the popular hike earlier this year to celebrate her 50th birthday in lieu of taking a quick, and cheaper, trip to Las Vegas - which is where she was thinking of celebrating, prior to the boycott.
Her favourite thing about the route in Spain, Mitchell added, is all the people she met along the way.
"Some people do the hike for personal reasons, and many of the people I talked to were in a transition," she said, adding that the hike had given her the chance to have "very lovely conversations with complete strangers".
Mitchell said she would be open to visiting the US again if a different president was in the White House, and if relations with Canada were restored.

The morning after an intoxicating D23 Friday night, which included a dancing spirit squad, Adam Driver and Inde Navarrette X-Men surprises, Josh Gad crooning, Ryan Gosling, Anne Hathaway and confetti raining, it became really clear — Disney is going to have a killer 2028 at the box office.
And they haven’t even filled out the entire year’s slate yet. With the 2026 domestic box office racking toward an estimated $10 billion stateside, will people still be going to the cinemas two years from now?
Hell yes, if Disney has anything to do with it.
Disney has 14 dates currently in the Rentrak system for 2028 — and that’s not counting 20th Century Studios or Searchlight theatrical releases. Again, dates can always shed, but with the few tentpole dates that were announced last night at D23’s The Ultimate Disney Fan Event at the Anaheim Honda Center, coupled with what we already know, it would not be shocking if 2028 has a shot at rivaling Disney’s record global year at the B.O., which was 2019 with $13.15B (that’s when they were fully merged with 20th Century Fox).
Watch on Deadline
Right now for 2028, if the studio can keep these productions on track, Disney has dated:
	Pixar original Ghost Market – March 10
Currently, no other wide release is dated against it. 
	Live-action Tangled – March 31
Amazon MGM Studios has a Chosen movie already on the schedule which is counter-programming to this highly anticipated feature adaptation of the 2010 animated pic. Tangled arrives in theaters a week ahead of Sony’s The Beatles – Four Films The Beginning on April 7, 2028.
	Marvel’s untiled X-Men – May 5
The MCU returns to its formerly prized summer launchpad, three years after 2025’s Thunderbolts*. Who dare date against this revival? In the hands of Feige, it’s not like Bryan Singer’s old stuff. From the looks of last night, per Hugh Jackman’s beam-in, he ain’t coming back as Wolverine.
	Live-action Lilo & Stitch 2  – Memorial Day weekend, May 28
Currently, Lionsgate has Resurrection of the Christ: Part Two on this date. Again, counter-programming skewing to an older adult religious demo. The two can co-exist, but depending on how successful Part One is (May 6, 2027), it would’t be shocking if Lionsgate changes their mind in the face of a five-quad sequel to a billion-dollar movie.
	
	Pixar’s Incredibles 3 – June 16
Before D23, Disney already announced the Fathers Day weekend date for the threequel to one of the highest grossing animated movies of all-time (Incredibles 2 at $1.2B). The kids—Violet, Dash and Jack Jack—are the same height, but grown up in their superhero abilities as the conceit here is that they sneak out of the house more. No other major studio pics are versing Incredibles 3 yet.
Marvel’s Ghost Rider – announced for 2028 without a specific date on the Gosling starring, Shawn Levy directed feature, but a good guess is that it’s going to July 28 that year as Disney has that weekend on hold in Rentrak. If it is July 28, well, that’s the penultimate end of summer date where Deadpool & Wolverine, Brand New Day and Fantastic Four: First Steps have soared. You’d be crazy to date against this movie.
	Marvel’s Black Panther 3 – Dec. 15, 2028
Clearly, the Christmas event movie of the year. Universal has an untitled tentpole dated five days later on Dec. 20. 
That’s quite a killer lineup on paper alone, and more powerful from what’s already on deck in 2027 for Disney, which we’ll sift through below. Here’s some takeaways from last night’s fireworks:
Marvel Cinematic Universe Movies Are No Longer in Superhero Fatigue
With three MCU titles dated for 2028, that’s absolutely clear, and with MCU Boss Kevin Feige involved in the success of Sony’s highest grossing movie of all-time, the Marvel Studios co-production Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $1.8B+, “It’s not about IP,” says one Disney executive talking about the success of that rival film. “It’s about making great movies. Spider-Man: Brand New Day isn’t successful because it’s a Spider-Man movie, it’s successful because it’s an excellent, fun movie.” That’s the plan for MCU going forward: Reliable and fun-filled filmmakers and talent like Ryan Gosling and Shawn Levy involved in Ghost Rider, and a murderers’ row of thespians in X-Men such as Driver, Obsession breakout Navarrette, Christopher Abbott and Samara Weaving, to name a few.
There was some cynicism from fans over the Avengers: Doomsday trailer that was released around San Diego Comic-Con, which is to be expected. You can’t spoil everything in a trailer for a highly anticipated sequel. Also, who isn’t going to watch this upside-down universe MCU movie where Iron Man‘s Robert Downey Jr. is Victor Werner von Doom? The clip released last night shows this is a more complex, sinister strategist than Josh Brolin’s crash-bang-boom baddie Thanos from the previous Avengers pics. Screams Pedro Pascal’s Reed Richards, “Answer me, Victor! Why did you do this?” Masses will want to know well into early 2027 in what’s an optimistic start to Disney’s 2027 box office year. Joker: Folie a Deux, this is not. And after the better-than-Barbenheimer success of The Odyssey and Brand New Day in the marketplace, it’s clear we won’t have a problem of two male fandom-charged properties like Doomsday and Dune: Part 3 getting in each other’s way. Both battalion boats will rise at the B.O.
	Live Action Takes Of Disney Classics Aren’t Going Away 
While Honda Center denizens last night could only get excited by less than a minute’s tease of Tangled, which showed Rapunzel’s long blonde hair and Kathryn Hahn briefly as notorious Mother Gothel, Disney isn’t bailing on bringing legacy animated classics into the flesh with even Moana recently falling off her surfboard with less than $300M at the global box office. Disney’s plan per sources going forward remains, of course, spacing out animated sequels from their live-action counterparts, as well as finding a unique way into beloved vault titles (i.e. a Bridesmaids-like spinoff of Cinderella from Akiva Schaefer with Stepsisters, not shown yesterday), the still-in-development punk rock Cruella 2 from Craig Gillespie starring Emma Stone, and the upcoming Beauty and the Beast-verse title, Gaston. Maleficent years ago was a great success for the studio. If that Sleeping Beauty spinoff taught Disney anything, it’s to approach live-action adaptations of the classics from the side in an edgy way rather than a full-on adaptation (i.e. Dumbo, Pinocchio, Snow White) with great filmmakers and sublime stars. Quite often, the old pics are dated in their morals and arrive with inherent themes which are more baggage than their worth for the studio when trying to pull in a pluralistic audience. Another lesson from Moana: Don’t make a carbon copy of the original animated pic. Better to vary it up with different musical numbers and deeper plots for fun’s sake. Also when it comes to non-Disney IP movies, the current motion picture administration is on the hunt for the next YA hit, which can easily fit into the Magic Kingdom’s sensibilities both spiritually and merchandising wise, read winning a big auction for Katherine Rundell’s Impossible Creatures, a publishing phenomenon on the order of Harry Potter, The Hunger Games and Twilight Saga (no updates yesterday).
	
	Animation Is Intact
With Frozen 3, a November 2029 date for Coco 2 and Incredibles 3, clearly Disney knows when it comes to making $1 billion hits, it never fails to make a sequel to a landmark hit. And ya gotta space ’em out. Frozen 3 arrives eight years after its previous chapter, Incredibles 3 is ten years later than its predecessor while Coco 2 will hit theaters 12 years after Coco. Disney kept their powder dry on what to expect on Coco 2 and Incredibles 3, showing very little footage. Essentially what we learned were plot reveals. 
Original Walt Disney Animation title, Hexed, due out at Thanksgiving, about a young woman coming into her bewitching powers while facing off against a coven, looks like it can work, elevating the leading independent female sensibility that the studio’s princess toons are known for, while also being the flip side of a Disney princess. Walton Goggins as a wisenheimer three-eyed Southern cat, Beef Roger Crummchuk, to Hailee Steinfeld’s protag, Billie Doe, is very funny and very Goggins. Disney vet Jodie Foster in her first Disney animation voiceover role as the villain, Queen Celeste, is intriguing. Well played, casting.
But get ready for Frozen 3. At the last D23 two years, they merely teased concept art, but this year, Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel (Anna and Elsa) rocked a new song, “Frozen Heart” while Josh Gad brought down the house with a new 1970s love song-sounding ditty about Olaf’s new g.f., “Samantha”. Add in a new black icy witch villain with powers that could topple Elsa and more about the ice sister’s past, and we got a great Star Wars-like film on our hands. The Jennifer Lee-directed threequel hits theaters on Nov. 24, 2027.
If you want to build franchises, you have to make originals, and as we know in the current post-Covid space, sometimes that means opening at a significantly lower gross and playing out. Pixar has always won in the original space when they do their own twist on a genre (i.e. space with Wall-E, French movies with Ratatouille) and anchor it on an emotionally affecting lead character. Not an easy needle to thread (Elio), but it appears they have something as they venture into horror with Ghost Market about a fast talking kid who has a supernatural interaction at a lunch shop hidden away in a remote location on Oʻahu’s North Shore that serves lost spirits, stuck between life and death.
	Mum’s the word on Avatar
There was no mention of the future of the Na’vi last night. Two movies remain on the release calendar, Avatar 4 for Dec. 21, 2029 and Avatar 5 for Dec. 19, 2031. As far as the fate of those pics, all we know is what franchise director James Cameron has said following the threequel’s $1.48 billion (the lowest in the franchise, but, hello, still an excellent gross for any movie). They’re “still floating out there.” 
	A New Hope for Star Wars?
Nothing new was announced, and this is the one label which requires the most resuscitation after Mandalorian and Grogu died this summer with $345M WW. Rather than getting lost in their heads on what to do with the Skywalkers or legacy characters after failing to take fans into hyperspace with 2018’s Solo: A Star Wars Story, Lucasfilm opted to go anew with elements that create alchemy, read the comedic and story awe of director Levy, scribe Jonathan Tropper and the cool and hysterically funny Gosling in Star Wars: Starfighter. It looks amazing, like Gosling’s Driver from Drive in space amid some new cool sea-filled planets. There’s an older mentor-to-kid story, and a nod to the drag race aura that George Lucas wove from his teen days into American Graffiti and Star Wars: Phantom Menace. For any die-hard Star Wars fans, there’s a lot of call-back in the imagery, but the question is whether they’ll buy into something completely fresh. The box office comp here isn’t Levy’s Deadpool & Wolverine ($211.4M domestic opening) which was working off a successful superhero comedy property, it’s more the spinoff of bigger IP, think 2016’s Fantastic Beasts coming off of Harry Potter ($74.4M domestic debut). There’s a lot of pressure on Levy and Gosling to truly take us to another galaxy far, far away next Memorial Day weekend.
Meanwhile, per newly appointed co-president, Dave Filoni, when it comes to an Adam Driver starring The Hunt for Ben Solo movies; fans, it’s not the movie you’re looking for, to quote Obi-wan Kenobi. Filoni told Deadline that when it comes to the next movie after Rise of Skywalker, “The force is not with us in that regard.”
This was the second time in the Disney fan confab’s history that they’ve wowed their future film and TV lineup at the Honda Centre (called D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event), taking what was once a filled theater-like presentation at the Anaheim Convention Center to what’s now an Ariana Grande-like concert spectacle with floating balloons, Broadway numbers and the entire arena doing “the wave” before the start of the show.
Too bad Marvel couldn’t pull it together and bring us Blade I must rather blade than Ghost Rider any day.

The year 2026 began on a strong note for India’s startup ecosystem, with Juspay becoming the first unicorn of the year within the first month of the year. The subsequent six months saw Sarvam, KreditBee, Skyroot Aerospace, Emergent, and Square Yards enter the unicorn club. In August, Astrotalk became the seventh startup to join the $1 Bn+ valuation club. At this pace, the Indian startup ecosystem is on track to mint about 10 unicorns this year – higher than 2025. However, this still is a far cry from the funding boom of 2021, when 45 startups entered the $1 Bn+ valuation club. The start of the funding winter in 2022 resulted in a sharp slowdown in unicorn creation over the subsequent years. While 22 startups turned unicorns in 2022, just two entered the unicorn club in 2023. The count increased in the subsequent year, with the startup ecosystem getting seven new unicorns in 2024. The unicorn trend mirrors a broader reset in startup funding. In 2025, Indian startups raised about $11 Bn across 936 deals, an 8% drop from the previous year, even as IPOs emerged as a key fundraising and liquidity route. Eighteen startups tapped public markets last year, raising nearly ₹20,000 Cr via fresh issues and delivering exits to early backers. While late stage private funding remained under pressure, growth stage investments rose 14% YoY, and investor interest increasingly shifted towards AI, deeptech and other long-term innovation-led sectors in 2025. With capital now flowing more selectively, founders and investors are shifting from a “growth-at-all-costs” mindset to a focus on sustainable business models and profitability. However, the Indian startup ecosystem continues to grow at a rapid pace. So far, 133 startups have entered the unicorn club. But the pace has shifted. What was once a unicorn frenzy has now become a more measured climb, as investors have become more selective. This has resulted in founders doubling down on fundamentals. While 16 of the 133 unicorns have since slipped below the $1 Bn valuation mark (some due to broader market volatility), others have taken different routes – 29 have gone public, while five have been acquired. As of August 2026, India’s unicorns have collectively raised over $118.5 Bn and command a combined valuation exceeding $396.6 Bn. Notably, among all the unicorns, Mensa Brands (now BRND.ME) took the least time to reach the billion-dollar mark; it achieved unicorn status in just six months. It was followed by GlobalBees, which took seven months to become a unicorn. Meanwhile, startups like Emergent, Ola Krutrim, and Glance took about a year to achieve unicorn status. The city’s position is backed by a mix of engineering talent, established investor networks, and consistent startup activity. The city led startup funding in 2025, attracting over $4.5 Bn capital, with companies like Razorpay, Meesho, Udaan, Rapido, Zepto, among others, raising substantial rounds. What’s notable is the continued concentration of new unicorns in the city. According to Inc42 analysis, eight out of the 10 startups that joined the unicorn club in 2024 and 2025 are headquartered in Bengaluru. Four of the seven new entrants in 2026 — Juspay, KreditBee, Emergent, and Sarvam — are headquartered in Bengaluru. Close behind, Delhi NCR and Mumbai take the second and third spots, with 42 and 18 unicorns, respectively. Meanwhile, other hubs are slowly coming into their own. Pune now boasts eight unicorns, benefitting from its product-first culture and talent pool. Chennai has produced five unicorns, anchored by strong manufacturing and SaaS roots. Hyderabad startup cohort, though smaller in count with three unicorns, continues to build quietly in deeptech and healthtech. Notably, Skyroot Aerospace is based in the city. Sectors Driving India’s Unicorn Boom Ecommerce, fintech, and enterprise tech continue to anchor India’s unicorn story. Of the 133 startups that have entered the unicorn club so far, 31 operate in ecommerce, 26 in fintech, and 20 in enterprise tech. But beyond the headline sectors, other categories are also seeing steady momentum. While consumer services has produced eight unicorns, sectors like media and entertainment, logistics, and edtech account for seven unicorns each, reflecting rising demand for digital content, last-mile delivery, affordable education, and everyday convenience. Travel tech and healthtech follow closely, with six unicorns each, indicating that Indian startups are also making strides in sectors driven by post-pandemic recovery, wellness, and global mobility. Meanwhile, with the entry of Skyroot, India also has a spacetech unicorn now. Emergent became the third AI unicorn, after Sarvama and Krutrim. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed on Saturday that his country struck the Progress Rocket Space Center deep within Russia using ground-launched cruise missiles.
“In Russia’s Samara region, one of the key enterprises within Roscosmos—the Progress Center, which was involved, among other things, in electronics production–was hit,” Zelenskyy said on the social media site X. “Flamingo missiles were used. A good achievement.”
The largest city in the Samara Oblast, about 900 km from the Ukrainian border, Samara is home to Russia’s most important manufacturer of rockets. The Progress center assembles the workhorse vehicle for Russia, the Soyuz-2 vehicle, as well as the newer Soyuz-5 rocket. The facility also builds military satellites.
Russia uses the Soyuz-2 rocket, which has a lift capacity of about 8 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, for a variety of civil and military purposes. Notably, it is the principal rocket used for Russia’s human spacecraft launches to the International Space Station.
Already a shortage of Soyuz rockets
It was not immediately clear which facilities at the sprawling Progress facility were damaged. There were some open-source reports that a missile struck a building that houses a clean room for avionics—perhaps a reference to the electronics production Zelenskyy referred to.

Indiana Jones franchise star Harrison Ford is bringing back his iconic adventurer for the first time since Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny in 2023.
Ford, of course, first appeared as Indy in Raiders of the Lost Ark — later renamed Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark — in 1981 before reprising the role for Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom in 1984 and Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade in 1989.
Then, in 2008, Ford reunited with the original trilogy’s director Steven Spielberg and writer-producer George Lucas for Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull. Ford took one final adventure as the legendary character under the direction of James Mangold with Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny.
While it seemed that The Dial of Destiny was Ford’s swan song for the role, he’s agreed to come back for another go-round as the gun-slinging and whip-wielding archaeologist for a role — as an animatronic Indy — in a project under construction at Walt Disney World’s Animal Kingdom theme park. According to Entertainment Weekly, plans were revealed Saturday night at Disney’s D23 convention in Anaheim, Calif., for the new Indy adventure, which is being built on the Dinoland U.S.A. attraction, which closed in 2025.
Harrison Ford Appears In A Video Announcement About The New ‘Indiana Jones’ Project
Harrison Ford made an announcement about the upcoming attraction — which is called Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent— via video Saturday night at D23.
In the video, Ford said, “Hello, D23, thanks for coming along on all of Indy’s adventures. Soon it will be time for his next ride, and I’m pleased to share for the first time ever, I’m the actual model for the Indiana Jones animatronic — fear of snakes included.”
Ford, 84, did not indicate when Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent would open, only to say that it would be “soon.” Disney did not indicate, either, whether the version of Indy for the ride will be from the original Indiana Jones movie trilogy or from the 2008 or 2023 film.
Indy was first brought to life at Walt Disney World’s Hollywood Studios theme park in 1989 with the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular! live show, where a stunt actor would play the daring adventurer in a recreation of his greatest action scenes from Raiders of the Lost Ark.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday extended support to a man who visited the government school in Bengal where he once studied, after his father was allegedly killed by BJP-linked goons for speaking out about the poor condition of government schools. In a post on X, Dipke shared a video of the injured man on a hospital bed and wrote, "Abdul went to inspect the govt school in Bengal where he once studied. He lost his father after they were attacked by goons (allegedly from BJP) for speaking up about the poor condition of govt schools. It makes my blood boil that people are being murdered simply for demanding better schools." Extending support to the victim, the CJP founder said, "CJP stands firmly with Abdul and his family. We demand the immediate arrest of those responsible for his father’s death. A CJP team will visit West Bengal and ensure that Abdul and his family get justice." Dipke also lashed out at the hatemongers and said, "And to the hatemongers who think they can silence us through violence: we are not going to back off. Attack our members, threaten us, try to intimidate us; we will only fight harder." He reiterated that the CJP will continue to fight for better schools and will not be silenced. According to Scroll, the incident took place in Karisunda village of Bankura district in West Bengal, with the local police confirming that a person had died. However, they claimed they had yet to receive a complaint regarding the same. On the contrary, the CJP alleged that when the volunteer, Abdul, approached the police to file a complaint, his request was denied. In a video shared on social media earlier this week, Abdul said he visited a primary school in Karisunda village to survey as part of the satirical outfit’s nationwide campaign to improve government schools in rural areas. He alleged that BJP workers later arrived at his home and assaulted him and his family, leaving his father with head injuries. This is a developing story. More details awaited. "Working class Joe. The only thing he worked over was the underage babysitter," one X post (archived) read.
The post featured an image purportedly showing Jill and Joe Biden alongside text that read:
This is Joe Biden at age 30 with his then 15 year old babysitter (while stil[l] married to his first wife)
The babysitter became his 2nd wife when she turned 18 three years later Her name is JILL BIDEN
In short, the claim that Jill Biden was a teenage babysitter for Joe Biden's children when they started dating is false. The couple met in 1975, after the death of Joe Biden's first wife, when Jill was in her 20s.
We previously fact-checked this claim in 2021 and 2025 when similar false rumors spread on social media.
How and when the Bidens first met
Jill Biden was born on June 3, 1951, and Joe Biden on Nov. 20, 1942, making them nearly nine years apart in age. Given this age difference, it would have been impossible for Joe Biden to be in his 30s while Jill Biden was still a teenager.
According to the White House website, Jill Biden met then-Senator Joe Biden in 1975. They married in 1977. In a 2016 Vogue interview, Jill stated that when she met Joe, she was a college senior. This means she was in her 20s at the time, not a teenager.
A Delaware Morning News article from July 17, 1977, detailed the origins of their relationship, stating that Joe Biden's brother, Frank, set them up on a blind date:
Son told Joe to marry Jill Jul 17, 1977 The Morning News (Wilmington, Delaware) Newspapers.com
In a 2012 CNN interview, when asked whether it was true that Joe Biden "set his eyes" on her after seeing a picture of her, Jill Biden recalled: "I had met him once before, and but we were in a crowd and it was at a fundraiser. So then I guess he saw my picture somewhere and he said 'oh, that's the kind of girl I'd like to date.' And I knew his brother, so his brother said 'oh, I know her.' Cause I was in college at the time and his brother was there. So Frank called me and, or got my number, and Joe called me. He said 'this is Joe Biden' and 'would you like to go out?'"
A 2020 campaign video titled "Get to Know Jill Biden" further corroborates this timeline. In it, Joe Biden recounts:
Joe Biden: My brother said, "There's this woman. You'll really like her, Joe." So I gave her a call. And she had a date that night.
Jill Biden: You said "Do you think you could break your date?"
Joe Biden: Oh, that's right. What did you do?
Jill Biden: "Well, I called and told the guy that I had a friend in from out of town and went out with Joe.
Joe Biden: I was 30. I was a senator. And I was a widower. Several years earlier, a tractor-trailer broadsided my wife and three children. My wife and daughter were killed. I wasn't big on the whole dating scene. But when I met Jill, I fell in love with her when I saw her.
"Those were the first words I spoke to Joe when he called me out of the blue on a Saturday in 1975," Jill wrote.
The Philadelphia Inquirer also published the photo with a caption credited to the Biden campaign, dating it to 1976. At the time, Jill would have been about 24, and Joe about 33. Joe Biden's first wife, Neilia Hunter Biden, had died in a car crash three years earlier.
Joe Biden's granddaughter Naomi Biden shared the image on X in November 2020, captioning it: "They've come a long, long, way together."
However, at least one version of the rumor circulating in August 2026 used what appeared to be a digitally distorted version of the same photograph.
Other rumors about Jill Biden that we have fact-checked in the past include the claim that she is not a medical doctor and is therefore wrongly using the title "Dr." and a rumor that she did not agree to marry Joe Biden until his fifth proposal.

How important is Community Shield to a team's season?
- Published
The Community Shield takes place between two teams who will be hoping to battle it out for the Premier League this season.
English champions Arsenal take on runners-up and FA Cup winners Manchester City at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Sunday.
But do the stats suggest winning the curtain-raiser in the Welsh capital would indicate a successful season ahead? And what of the goalscorers?
- Why is the Community Shield being held in Wales? 
  - Published21 July
Do Community Shield winners usually win the Premier League?
Considering the current Premier League champions play in the game every season it is surprisingly rare for the Community Shield winners to go on to win the league.
Since the Premier League started in 1992-93, only eight of the 34 winners of the Charity or Community Shield have done so.
Five of those happened in a six-year spell from 2005 until 2010.
Manchester City, in 2019, were the last team to do so - and before that it was Alex Ferguson's Manchester United in 2011.
Only one of the past 15 winners of the Community Shield have gone on to become champions that season.
Since 1992 the teams who lose the Community Shield have won more league titles that season - 10 in total, including Manchester City for three years in a row between 2021 and 2023.
Last year Crystal Palace beat Liverpool and ended up finishing 15th, although they did go on to win the Conference League. The Reds also had a disappointing domestic campaign, finishing fifth.
Some 47% of the time (16/34) the upcoming season's Premier League winners had not been involved in the Community Shield - like Arsenal in 2025-26.
And 53% of the time (18/34) the Shield winners have finished above the losers in the league that season.
On 10 occasions the two teams have finished as the top two in the Premier League - with four of those times being the Shield winners top and the losers as runners-up.
Do Premier League winners usually win Community Shield?
The other question is how many Community Shields are won by the previous season's Premier League winners.
The answer is 18 out of 34 times - so 53%.
But in recent times it has become less frequent. Including Crystal Palace, the FA Cup winners have won eight of the past 12 Shields, something that had only happened five times in the previous 22.
And on three occasions in the Premier League era, neither the league nor cup winners have won it.
Arsenal (1999 and 2023) and Manchester United (2010) qualified as Premier League runners-up and beat the Double winners in the game.
Do Community Shield goalscorers go on to have good seasons?
This one is a bit of a mixed bag.
Crystal Palace's 2025 scorers Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr netted 37 goals between them last season.
Hugo Ekitike scored his first of 17 goals in his debut season for Liverpool - but Jeremie Frimpong did not enjoy a great first campaign after netting.
In 2023 Cole Palmer netted for Manchester City in their game against Arsenal (a match they would go on to lose on penalties after Leandro Trossard's injury-time equaliser).
He would go on to score 22 Premier League goals and be named young player of the season... for Chelsea, having joined them for £42.5m.
The previous season, Darwin Nunez scored on his Liverpool debut - and Erling Haaland failed to notch on his City bow.
That led to post-match discussion about Nunez looking the better player.
However, Haaland went on to 52 goals that season, with Nunez netting only 15.
Kelechi Iheanacho only scored four Premier League goals after his 2021 Community Shield winner.
But back in 2019 Raheem Sterling's Shield strike for City against former club Liverpool kick-started the most productive season of his career (31 goals).

Lions and tigers begin a long-awaited rescue from a notorious Argentine zoo
Thirty lions and tigers from a closed Argentine zoo are starting a new life at wildlife sanctuaries in South Africa and the United States
LUJAN, Argentina -- Thirty lions and tigers that were kept alive — barely — for years in cramped concrete cages at a shuttered Argentine zoo began entering jumbo-size transport crates Friday as they embarked on ambitious journeys to wildlife sanctuaries halfway across the world in South Africa and the United States.
The cats are being rescued from the former Luján Zoo, about 70 kilometers (43 miles) northwest of Argentina's capital of Buenos Aires, after years of uncertainty over their fate. Four Paws, the international animal-welfare organization overseeing the transfer, described it as one of the largest relocations of captive big cats in the world.
“We are putting everything into making this go as smoothly as possible so we can celebrate that 30 lives have improved because of this effort,” said Luciana D’Abramo, program director for Four Paws.
Once loaded into their crates and placed aboard cargo and passenger jets, nine tigers and six lions will be flown to Lionsrock, a Four Paws sanctuary in South Africa that houses more than 80 big cats across natural enclosures sprawling 60 hectares (148 acres). The remaining eight tigers and seven lions will travel to The Wild Animal Sanctuary in Colorado, a vast refuge on the grasslands northeast of Denver where rescued lions, tigers and other animals roam expansive habitats.
But getting there is no easy feat: The big cats bound for Colorado will fly through Chile, while the others will travel to Johannesburg via Frankfurt or Amsterdam before a four-hour drive to Lionsrock.
The Four Paws handlers trained many of the lions and tigers to enter the crates voluntarily. But some of the big cats required sedation, including two tigers that veterinarians hoisted in canvas slings Friday and carried by hand to their transport crates.
Argentine authorities shut down the Lujan Zoo — famous for letting visitors handle and pose for pictures with tigers and lions — over safety and animal welfare concerns in 2020. D’Abramo said about 200 big cats were living there when it closed. Only 112 remained when Four Paws first arrived in 2023 seeking a solution.
By the time the organization was allowed to take over the site two years later, that number had fallen to 62. Some of the captive animals can barely walk because of obesity, muscle loss or poor nutrition. Others suffer from dental and kidney disease, complications from declawing and injuries that never healed properly.
“That alone shows the level of overcrowding and the conditions in which these animals have endured,” D’Abramo said.
The organization retrained longtime zoo employees in modern animal-welfare practices and began improving the cats’ diets and medical care. This transfer leaves more than 20 lions and tigers at Luján while Four Paws searches for their long-term homes.

The Income Tax Department on Saturday notified a new voluntary disclosure scheme allowing small taxpayers to declare certain undisclosed foreign assets and income by paying an effective 60 per cent tax, as the government seeks to bring overseas holdings into the tax net without exposing eligible taxpayers to further penalties or prosecution.
The Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), announced in the 2026-27 Budget, will take effect from August 16, with online declarations open until December 31, 2026, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) said.
The scheme is aimed at taxpayers such as students, young professionals, technology employees and relocated non-resident Indians who may have failed to disclose eligible foreign assets or income.
Under the rules, taxpayers will pay 30 per cent tax on the value of the declared undisclosed foreign asset or income, plus an additional amount equal to the tax, effectively taking the levy to 60 per cent. The fair market value of assets will be determined as of March 31, 2026, the CBDT said.
There are two categories of declarations under FAST-DS. For an undisclosed foreign asset or foreign income that was not previously offered to tax, the aggregate value must not exceed Rs 1 crore.
A second category covers foreign assets that were already offered to tax or acquired when the taxpayer was a non-resident but were not reported in the relevant tax-return schedule. The threshold for such declarations is Rs 5 crore, with a Rs 1 lakh fee payable.
The CBDT said the scheme is intended to enable eligible taxpayers to disclose “certain undisclosed foreign assets, undisclosed foreign income, or undeclared foreign assets” on payment of the specified tax or fee.
For example, where an undisclosed foreign bank account is valued at Rs 60 lakh and undisclosed foreign income amounts to Rs 20 lakh, the total tax payable would be Rs 48 lakh, according to an example in the CBDT’s frequently asked questions.
Taxpayers making valid declarations will receive immunity from any further tax or penalty and from prosecution under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, in respect of the assets or income disclosed.
The declared income or the amount invested in the disclosed asset will also not be included in the taxpayer’s total income under the Income-tax Act, 1961 or the Black Money Act, the CBDT said.
Notifying the rules for the scheme, the CBDT said the scheme “enables eligible taxpayers to declare certain undisclosed foreign assets, undisclosed foreign income, or undeclared foreign assets, on payment of a specified tax or fee”.

One of the big tradeoffs with Xteink’s pocket-friendly e-readers is a lack of easy access to ebooks. On a Kindle or Kobo you can download tens of thousands of titles through each device’s respective online bookstores, but with Xteink’s devices you have to source DRM-free ebooks on your own. That’s about to change, as the developers of CrossPoint Reader, a free alternative firmware for the X3, X4, and X4 Pro, are introducing support for third-party plug-ins that will expand the e-readers’ capabilities. One of the first from the community will give the devices access to DRM-protected ebooks borrowed through OverDrive’s Libby library app, or purchased through bookstores like Kobo’s.
Xteink’s tiny e-readers are getting access to free books through Libby
The CrossPoint Reader firmware is getting plug-ins that add support for ebooks from Libby, Kobo, and other sources.
The new functionality is still in beta, but while the team behind CrossPoint Reader provided me with custom firmware I’ve been testing on the X4 Pro for the past few days, it’s now available to anyone who wants to try it. Getting ebooks from Libby onto the tiny e-readers isn’t as streamlined as using its mobile app or as simple as Kobo’s native OverDrive support, but it’s much easier than I expected. If you’re already comfortable with wirelessly transferring files to your tiny e-reader, loading ebooks from Libby isn’t much harder.
The first step is saying good riddance to the frustrating stock firmware on Xteink’s devices and installing the free CrossPoint Reader alternative. The easiest approach is to connect your e-reader to your computer with its USB-C cable, power it on, and then flash the new firmware directly through a browser using the CrossPoint Reader website that lets you select your specific device and which version of the firmware you want.
You then need to download and install CrossPoint Reader’s new Plugin Store, which is available here. Installation is as simple as unzipping a few files onto your e-reader’s microSD card, which will put a new Plugins section on the e-reader’s homescreen. It’s currently populated with a few different tools you can download, but the important one to install is the “Protected Content” plug-in. It runs through CrossPoint Reader’s built-in web server (which is probably much easier to use than you think) and allows Xteink’s devices to access ebooks protected by the Adobe Digital Editions DRM.
To get it all working you’ll need a free ByteBooks account (or you can convert an older Adobe Digital Editions account you haven’t touched in years) so you can login and authorize your e-reader to open DRM-protected ebooks. You’ll also need access to Libby itself on another device, which requires a library card to sign in. For several reasons, including the fact that Xteink’s devices use low-power ESP-32 processors, you’re not able to search or download ebooks from Libby directly on the e-readers themselves.
Once you borrow a book the Libby apps will let you download it as a protected EPUB file. What you’re actually downloading first is a tiny ACSM file that an authorized reading app uses to access the DRM-protected ebook file. The new “Protected Content” plug-in running through the CrossPoint Reader web server processes an ACSM file moved to the microSD card, downloads a copy of the book, and copies the EPUB file to your e-reader, where you can read it for as long as the loan allows.
The process is similar for ebooks purchased from stores like Kobo’s that use the EPUB format with ADE. (Amazon doesn’t.) When logged into Kobo’s website (not the desktop app) you can download an ACSM file for a book you’ve purchased, copy it to your Xteink device, and then process it with the plug-in to access the ebook you can actually read.
If you want to simplify the Libby process, you can instead download and install an app called Common Stacks (available for Android, Windows, and macOS, with iOS support coming soon) that’s designed to provide access to multiple free ebook libraries, including ones you host yourself. The app includes full access to Libby and can both download and send ebook files directly to Xteink’s e-readers with just a couple of clicks. Common Stacks also relies on CrossPoint Reader’s web server functionality running in the back end, but getting borrowed books onto the X4 Pro was as easy as borrowing library books on my Kobo is.
While Libby and Common Stacks is one of the best ways to get free ebooks onto Xteink’s devices, you’ll want to be mindful that selection will vary from library to library, and you may occasionally have to wait to download a popular title depending on how many digital copies are available or are already loaned out. However, now that Xteink’s tiny e-readers finally have access to DRM-protected ebooks — whether borrowed or bought — they’re an even more tempting alternative to Kindles and Kobos.
