How to Use AI to Prepare for a Job Interview
Before we get to the applications, which indeed make job interview preparation an easy affair, you must understand the importance of a solid foundation to begin with. Fortunately, this groundwork only requires leveraging existing AI tools you may already be using. After getting to know the details of the job interview, mainstream AI models, such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, and more, can be directed to put you at an advantage from the very initial phase of your preparation. Below is what you must do first.
→ Understand the Role and Generate Role-Specific Interview Questions
Most, if not all, job descriptions are little more than a pile of technical and corporate jargon, often failing to clearly state the requirements. Misaligned interview expectations may already put you in a bad spot during the interview, so you must ensure that you are well-versed with the job description. AI models can help you do so with a few prompts, but you must include a few crucial elements to get the best results. With all this, don’t forget to upload your updated resume for a tailored response.
For starters, you cannot miss out on knowing the core competencies required for the job you’re applying for. AI can help you identify the top non-negotiable technical and soft skills that the recruiter expects of you. Such attributes are often not understood by many applicants, which prevents them from brushing up on existing skills or learning the required ones. Next, your prompt must include identifying the success metrics, or the key performance indicators of the role.
Because every hiring takes place to solve a specific problem of the organization, it’s crucial to have an idea about the performance expectations the recruiter may have from you. For tech roles, it usually revolves around solving existing issues, improving existing processes, and related tasks. In contrast, non-tech roles focus on increasing client retention, establishing business relationships, and related tasks.
Lastly, you must also ask AI to groom you based on your resume. It will help you determine whether your resume aligns well with the role and whether any specific skills need to be spotlighted. AI can not only identify potential loopholes but also help you present your projects to the interviewer in the most convincing way possible. With this initial study of the role’s requirements, you can certainly answer questions and defend yourself with confidence.
→ Study About the Company
While most candidates think they know the company they’re applying to well, the truth is, not many perform a proper deep dive. It is an important part of interview preparation, as knowing the company helps you give more relevant answers instead of generic ones.
AI makes company research much easier, but don’t simply ask it to “tell me about the company.” Start with its current market position, products, competitors, recent announcements, and anything else directly relevant to the role.
Foremost, your prompt should include information about the company’s current market position. You can assist the AI model by attaching the company’s press releases, financial reports, product launch notes, public announcements, and more. Financial reports can also be used to project the company’s future trends, map future goals, and more, which are worth knowing about.
It’s also essential to understand the company’s competitors, as it can help you frame your answers to interview questions in the company’s favor. While you are unlikely to find many, you can ask the AI model to identify and propose viable solutions to the company’s publicly available problems. It can be a significant advantage when handled appropriately and also serves as a good background for obvious questions, such as “What will you bring to the table?” and “Why should we hire you?”
→ Analyze the Interviewer
If you know who will be interviewing you, publicly available professional information can help you prepare better. Their LinkedIn profile, current role, past experience, or area of expertise may give you a fair idea of which parts of your background they are more likely to focus on.
You can provide this information to an AI model and ask it to suggest questions that someone in a similar role may ask. Don’t treat those questions as predictions, though. Use them simply to broaden your preparation and identify areas you may otherwise overlook.
This information is also useful when preparing questions to ask towards the end of the interview. Relevant questions about their team, role, or experience with the company will usually come across better than generic ones.
→ Generate Behavioral, Situational, and Technical Interview Questions
A recommended way to ensure success in an interview is to prepare for the likely questions. The question set should not only include the basic ones, but also challenging ones to put you on the spot. That way, your real-world performance will be sufficient for selection. To begin with, the basics: you can ask AI models to generate common behavioral interview questions, such as “Introduce yourself” and “Why should we hire you?” “What if we don’t select you?” “What makes you fit for this role?” and the like.
The answers to the above questions will be based on your resume and cognitive ability, which is what AI models can help you with. Next, to tackle the technical questions, your prompt must instruct the AI model to fire deep-dive technical, situational, and project-based questions at you. During all this, you can rate your technical skills and promptly improve any weak areas.
Despite the discomfort, ask the AI model to generate questions from the perspective of an interviewer who is not interested in hiring you. Understand the questions, as they can prove to be great at identifying gaps in your resume, incompetencies, and more. You can also ask the AI model to question the relevance of your past experiences, push back aggressively on your answers, and more. This will only improve your chances of getting selected.
→ Practice Mock Interviews With AI Voice Mode
In case you are unaware, most mainstream AI models offer voice modes that are perfect for back-and-forth questioning, making them ideal for interview practice. It’s not surprising that merely reading the questions and thinking you can answer them won’t cut it, which is why you need a simulation of the interview. It may cause you to memorize answers instead of coming up with your own, which may result in you sounding like a teleprompter, or worse, freezing on the spot if you forget the exact answer, leaving a bad impression.
Voice mode is best used on the mobile versions of AI agents. First, you must tell the AI its persona by verbally describing it, uploading the job description, interview details, or any other supporting documents. We also recommend uploading your resume to ensure a curated interaction. Next, you must instruct it to ask all types of questions, including behavioral, technical, and situation-based.
Remember, the purpose of this mock interview is to prepare you for the worst, so take away critical lessons and improve yourself. For this, you can ask the AI model to rate your answers and provide you with detailed assessments to help you identify your weak points. Not only will it cure the interview phobia that you may have, but it will also improve your speaking skills, conversational awareness, and your ability to answer curveballs.

Useful AI Prompts for Job Interview Preparation
Mainstream AI models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude can be surprisingly effective for interview preparation if you give them enough context. A common approach among job seekers is to provide the actual job description and resume, then have the AI conduct the interview one question at a time instead of generating a generic list of questions. Here are a few prompts worth trying.
1. Analyze the Job Description and My Resume
I am preparing for an interview for the job below. Act as an experienced hiring manager and analyze both the job description and my resume.
Identify:
The five most important skills or requirements for this role
The parts of my resume that match them best
Important requirements where my experience looks weak or unclear
Questions an interviewer is likely to ask about those gaps
Technical or industry topics I should revise
Five achievements from my resume that I should make sure to highlight
Don’t invent experience or skills that aren’t present in my resume.
Job description: [paste]
Resume: [paste/upload]
2. Conduct a Realistic Mock Interview
Act as the hiring manager interviewing me for the role below. Use my resume and the job description as your primary context.
Conduct this like a real interview. Ask only one question at a time and wait for my complete answer before asking the next one. Ask natural follow-up questions based on what I actually say instead of following a fixed list.
Include a mix of behavioral, situational, resume-based, role-specific, and technical questions where relevant.
Do not give me hints or feedback while the interview is taking place. Once the interview is finished, score my performance on answer quality, relevance, clarity, confidence, and completeness. Then identify my five biggest weaknesses and tell me how to improve each one.
Job description: [paste]
Resume: [paste/upload]
3. Give Me a Difficult Mock Interview
Act as a skeptical interviewer who isn’t yet convinced that I am the right person for this role.
Use my resume and the job description to identify weak points, career gaps, vague achievements, missing skills, questionable claims, or areas where another candidate may be stronger.
Ask me one difficult question at a time. If my answer is vague, generic, evasive, or unsupported, push back and ask a follow-up question. Don’t compliment every answer or make the interview artificially easy.
At the end, tell me which answers could hurt my chances in the real interview and show me how I could make them stronger without exaggerating my experience.
4. Build My STAR Interview Stories
Help me prepare 5 reusable stories from my career for behavioral interview questions.
Use my resume and the experiences I provide to identify strong examples involving leadership, conflict, failure, problem-solving, teamwork, initiative, and working under pressure.
For each story, organize the answer using STAR:
Situation: What was happening?
Task: What was I responsible for?
Action: What specifically did I do?
Result: What changed because of my actions?
Keep Situation and Task brief and spend more time on Action and Result. Ask me for missing details rather than inventing them. Where possible, help me quantify the result.
Finally, tell me which common behavioral interview questions each story could answer.
Excel in Interviews With These AI Tools
AI has made preparing for job interviews a lot less daunting than it used to be. For most people, mainstream AI models such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are already good enough for understanding a job description, researching a company, preparing likely questions, and improving answers.
Dedicated AI interview tools become useful when you want something closer to the real thing. Exponent Practice and Interviewing.io make more sense for technical candidates, Yoodli is particularly good for communication and behavioral practice, while MyInterviewAI works well for resume-based preparation. Whichever tool you choose, don’t stop after one mock interview. Upload your latest resume and the actual job description, complete a practice session, review where you struggled, and repeat it after fixing those areas. Two or three focused mock interviews will be far more useful than memorizing dozens of AI-generated answers.
Critique My Interview Answer
I will give you an interview question followed by my answer.
Evaluate the answer as a demanding hiring manager. First, tell me:
Whether I actually answered the question
What was convincing
What sounded vague or generic
Whether I gave enough evidence
Whether I spent too much time on irrelevant context
What follow-up question an interviewer would probably ask
If it is a behavioral question, also evaluate it using the STAR method.
Only after giving me this critique, provide a stronger version that retains my real experience and sounds natural when spoken aloud. Don’t turn it into a polished corporate script that nobody would actually say in an interview.
FAQs about AI Interview Tools
Can ChatGPT help me prepare for a job interview?
Yes. You can give ChatGPT your resume and job description and ask it to identify likely interview questions, evaluate your answers, conduct mock interviews, research the role, and point out gaps in your preparation. Voice mode makes the mock interview experience significantly more natural.
Are AI mock interviews actually useful?
They can be, especially when the AI asks follow-up questions and gives detailed feedback instead of simply generating a list of questions. They are particularly useful for repeated practice, although they shouldn't completely replace practice with another person when that is available.
Which AI interview tools are free?
Exponent Practice offers a limited number of free peer mock interviews, while Yoodli has a free tier. Huru AI provides free access to try its mock interviews, and Ophy AI offers free starting credits. The exact limits can change, so check each service before signing up.
What is the best AI interview tool for software engineers?
Interviewing.io and Exponent Practice are the strongest options on this list for software engineers. They focus much more heavily on coding, system design, algorithms, and other technical interview formats than general-purpose interview coaching tools.
Can I use AI during an actual job interview?
That depends entirely on the employer and interview rules. Some companies prohibit outside assistance during interviews and assessments. Unless the interviewer explicitly allows it, the safer approach is to use AI extensively during preparation and answer the actual interview questions yourself.
How many AI mock interviews should I practice?
There is no fixed number. Instead of repeating mock interviews endlessly, complete one, review the feedback, fix the weak areas, and try again. A few focused sessions with clear improvement between them are more useful than doing many interviews without reviewing your mistakes.

A chain of private plasma donation clinics in Canada said Friday it is pausing collections after the deaths of two donors and a new government investigation into potential unsafe practices.
Grifols, the Spanish healthcare company that runs 17 clinics across Canada and is the country’s only private clinic for plasma donation, said it informed Health Canada of its decision to temporarily pause collections on Wednesday.
That same day, the agency had issued a formal notice of non-compliance for failure to follow blood regulations, a senior official told the Globe and Mail newspaper.
The two deaths occurred after plasma donations in October 2025 and January 2026, Health Canada said in March of this year. The donors, both of whom were in the province of Manitoba, went into “distress” while donating, people familiar with the cases said.
Though Health Canada did not release the identities of the donors, friends said one was Rodiyat Alabede, 22, an international student and aspiring social worker who donated plasma in Winnipeg on 25 October.
Patient advocates reported at the end of May that there were concerns about whether Alabede had been properly screened.
“They had staff taking plasma from donors who did not know how to extract plasma in a safe manner,” alleged Kat Lanteigne, a safe blood campaigner who represents Alabede’s family.
“The [failures] were so egregious that … now we have more questions than answers,” she said in May.
An autopsy showed Alabede died of cardiac arrest shortly after donating. Health Canada reported that it found “no link” between Alabede’s death and plasma donation.
Patient advocates have called for a new inquest into her death, however, after alleging that “significant medical discrepancies” had been uncovered between her autopsy, which was completed two days after her death, and the medical summary drafted by Health Canada published on 27 March of this year.
The Guardian has also seen Health Canada inspection reports from May that found multiple deficiencies at Grifols clinics, including inadequate training for staff, failures in standard operating procedures, poor record keeping and a failure by Grifols to remedy past issues.
The Health Canada report also found that staff did not stop plasma collection when alarms went off, and described the company’s reporting as “incomplete” and “inaccurate”.
Prior to the newly announced pause, donations were permitted at Grifols twice a week. The company paid donors up to C$100 (£55) for each donation.
Plasma is a pale yellow, protein-rich liquid in blood that assists in moving red and white blood cells, along with platelets, through blood vessels, according to Canadian Blood Services, the non-profit that operates Canada’s national blood supply.
Plasma also helps prevent excessive bleeding and is used to create medications for a variety of conditions including hemophilia, liver disease and various cancers.
The plasma donation process differs from donating blood overall. A medical device called an apheresis machine draws the blood, separates it into individual parts, collects the components needed and then returns the remaining blood back into the body, according to Canadian Blood Services. The process takes about 90 minutes, whereas a general blood draw takes about 10.
In Canada, provinces and territories decide whether paid plasma clinics are permitted. British Columbia and Quebec do not allow the practice, for example, but Manitoba, where the deaths occurred, does not prohibit companies from paying donors for plasma.
Grifols said it decided to pause collection “proactively and voluntarily” due to what it deemed “unfounded attention.” It said the pause would allow it to work with Health Canada and Canadian Blood Services.
The company has denied the two deaths were connected to plasma donation.
On Friday, Health Canada said it found “various deficiencies” specifically at the Taylor Avenue Grifols location in Winnipeg. A spokesperson for that location said it’s working closely with the company so that it can return to operations.
“Canadians can be assured that this decision will have no impact on the safety and security of Canada’s blood and plasma supply,” Grifols said.

Scheffler in charge as he chases first win since January
- Published
St Jude Championship - round three leaderboard
-13 S Scheffler (US); -11 S Burns (US), Im (Kor); -8 J Knapp (US), T Fleetwood (Eng)
Selected others: -7 B Harman (US); -6 V Hovland (Nor); -5 W Clark (US); -4 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), J Spieth (US); -3 L Aberg (Swe); -2 H Hall (Eng); -1 A Rai (Eng); +6 J Rose (Eng), R McIlroy (NI)
World number one Scottie Scheffler will take a two-stroke lead into the final round of the St Jude Championship as he chases his first victory since January.
Scheffler, 30, carded a two-under 68 on Saturday to sit at 13 under overall, with his American compatriot Sam Burns at 11 under alongside South Korea's Im Sung-jae.
Burns produced a superb bogey-free 62 to move into contention in the FedEx Cup play-off opener at TPC Southwind in Memphis.
England's Tommy Fleetwood, who is the defending FedEx Cup champion, is a further three strokes adrift at eight under with Jake Knapp.
And it ensures an intriguing fourth round, with close friends Scheffler and Burns in the final pairing.
"Strategy is still the same, just go out there and execute," said Scheffler, who last led an event after 54 holes at the 2025 Open Championship.
"This is a golf course where that's really all it comes down to. It's always a little weird just because I want him to have success so much and I think he wants the same for me.
"It will be a competition like normal. It will be fun being out there with your friend but it's also a bit weird."
Sweden's Alex Noren and Norway's Viktor Hovland are well placed for strong finishes at seven and six under respectively.
However, six-time major winner Rory McIlroy and 2013 US Open champion Justin Rose both faltered badly on the 18th hole to sit well off the pace at six over.
Northern Ireland's McIlroy carded a double-bogey six after driving into the water off the tee, while Rose fared even worse finding the same hazard twice on his way to a triple-bogey seven.
The top 50 players in the FedEx standings at the end of the weekend will advance into next week's BMW Championship, with the top 30 after that advancing to the Tour Championship.

MacKenzie Scott, ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has become one of the most influential philanthropists in America by pioneering large-scale medical debt relief. According to a report by Fortune, through her donations to Undue Medical Debt (formerly known as RIP Medical Debt) Scott helped transform a small non-profit into a national force. Since 2020, her gifts totalling more than. $100 million have enabled the organisation to abolish more than $40 billion medical debt across all 50 states, providing relief to millions of families. The initiative of cutting down the medical debt is a small part of Scott’s larger philanthropic footprint. After her divorce from Bezos, Scott was left with a 4% stake in Amazon which she sold down over time. Scott has also given away more than $26 billion to more than 2,500 organisations which include Black colleges and universities, environmental groups, and economic equity nonprofits and more. As per Fortune report, the recent estimates suggest that her net worth stands at around $33.8 billion.
How MacKenzie Scott managed to abolish the medical debt of $40 billion
The model introduced by Scott is simple but powerful. The hospitals and physician groups routinely sell uncollectible patient debt in bulk portfolios at steep discounts. Instead of debt collectors buying these portfolios, Undue Medical Debt steps in as the buyer. With donations, it acquires the debt at pennies on the dollar and then abolishes it entirely. 
The math is striking: every $10 donated erases roughly $1,000 in patient debt. This arbitrage between distressed debt markets and healthcare dysfunction has created one of the most effective philanthropic models in recent years.
McKenzie Scott’s approach also inspired other billionaires
The model introduced by Scott also inspired other billionaires. Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and his wife Miranda Kerr recently donated millions to the nonprofit, erasing $550 million in medical bills for 261,000 Californians. Hedge fund billionaire Daniel Och’s family foundation cleared $264 million in Miami-Dade, while New York City and Cook County, Illinois, have used public funds to retire hundreds of millions more. The largest single deal came in April 2025, when Undue Medical Debt retired a $30 billion portfolio, wiping out obligations for 20 million people.
A model with limits
Even with MacKenzie Scott's outsized role in scaling the movement, the philanthropic momentum is unfolding against a backdrop of stalled policy reform. A Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that would have removed medical debt from the credit reports of 15 million Americans was vacated on July 11, 2025, by U.S. District Judge Sean Jordan of the Eastern District of Texas, who ruled it exceeded the CFPB's authority and violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act. No federal medical debt cancellation legislation has advanced through Congress since.
That gap between philanthropic scale and policy inaction is central to how critics view the model's limits. Even Undue Medical Debt's $40 billion in total relief, made possible in large part by Scott's early and sustained backing, represents only a fraction of the estimated medical debt held by American households nationwide. Closing that broader gap through voluntary giving alone would likely require a sustained, decades-long commitment, one that also depends on continued access to a distressed debt market that may not always offer the same steep discounts it does today.
MacKenzie Scott’s approach shows how billionaire philanthropy can offer immediate relief to millions, but it also underscores a larger reality: lasting change may require systemic reforms that address why medical debt becomes a burden in the first place.

An Indian court has sentenced a high-profile former editor of an investigative news magazine to 10 years in prison after convicting him of raping a junior colleague, overturning his acquittal in a case that drew nationwide attention.
Tarun Tejpal, 63, the founder and former editor of Tehelka magazine, was accused of raping a journalist in the lift of a five-star hotel in the western coastal state of Goa during an event in November 2013. He was arrested and spent seven months in jail until the supreme court granted him bail.
A court in Goa acquitted Tejpal of charges including rape, sexual harassment and wrongful restraint in 2021.
The government of Goa challenged the acquittal before the Bombay high court, which set aside the trial court’s verdict and sentenced him to 10 years in jail on Thursday.
“He has been convicted to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. He has been given two weeks’ time to surrender,” the police investigator Sunita Sawant, who led the case against Tejpal, told reporters.
The court also ordered him to pay a £3,900 fine, he said.
Tejpal, 63, said he would challenge the conviction in the supreme court.
He had initially blamed the assault on “a lapse of judgement” but later alleged the case against him was part of a vendetta by the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) government in Goa.
“For the past 13 years, they have been pursuing me as a part of a political vendetta,” he said after conviction.
Sawant told reporters: “This is a sentence where a girl has stood up for her rights … so this judgment is very important for women who are working in any sector.”
The case emerged at a time when India’s handling of sexual assault cases was under intense scrutiny after the gang-rape and murder of a 23-year-old student on a Delhi bus in December 2012.
That attack triggered nationwide protests and international outrage, and prompted the government to strengthen the country’s rape laws.
Tejpal’s case severely damaged the authority and credibility of Tehelka, which had historically championed women’s rights and social justice.
The magazine continues to operate under new leadership, but it has failed to regain the influence it had before the 2013 case.

Slipknot is officially parting ways with Sid Wilson, who had been part of the group for nearly 30 years.
“Effective immediately, Slipknot will no longer be associated with Sid Wilson,” the band posted on its Instagram account in a post that has since been taken down. “We wish him the best in his future endeavors.”
The DJ and keyboardist had been part of the heavy metal group since 1998, a year before Slipknot’s first studio album was released.
News of Wilson’s departure was first reported by TMZ in late July, although the reason that Slipknot decided to kick him out remains unclear. That same day, Slipknot guitarist Jim Root posted a message on his Instagram story set to the band’s 2008 song “‘Til We Die.”
Popular on Variety
“Don’t believe everything you read,” Root wrote. “Stop. Think. Take a breath. Sit with it for awhile. Maybe. Just maybe even wait until there’s more information.”
Wilson’s exit comes after Craig Jones left the band in 2023 and Chris Fehn left in 2019. Joey Jordison died in 2021, while Paul Gray died in 2020. Slipknot’s albums include “Slipknot,” “Iowa,” “Vol. 3,” “All Hope Is Gone,” “.5: The Gray Chapter,” “We Are Not Your Kind” and “The End, So Far,” which was released in 2022.
The band’s most recent live performance was in July 2025 at Inkcarceration, a music and tattoo festival in Ohio.
The remaining members of Slipknot have yet to speak out about Wilson’s sudden departure and what it means for the future of the band.

Telangana currently has 36 government institutions offering more than 4,400 MBBS seats, but only four of its government medical colleges have found a place among the top 144 government medical institutions in the country in the latest International Institutional Ranking Framework (IIRF) 2026 rankings.
The rankings, which assess higher education institutions across several academic and institutional parameters, have placed Gandhi Medical College, Secunderabad as the highest-ranked government medical college from Telangana at 43rd position. Osmania Medical College, Hyderabad, followed at 52nd position, while Kakatiya Medical College, Warangal, was ranked 60th. Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), Adilabad, was placed much lower at 139th position.
At the national level, the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, secured the first position among government medical institutions.
Private colleges: 18 Telangana institutions in top 187
The representation of Telangana was considerably higher in the private medical colleges category. Of the 187 private medical colleges included in the IIRF list, 18 institutions from Telangana featured in the rankings. The State currently has 29 private medical colleges, collectively offering around 5,850 MBBS seats.
The top position in the private medical colleges category was secured by Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore.
The rankings therefore present a contrasting picture for the State. While its established government institutions such as Gandhi Medical College and Osmania Medical College feature within the upper half of the national government medical colleges list, a large number of newer government medical colleges established during the State’s recent expansion of medical education do not feature among the 144 ranked institutions.
Three Telangana dental colleges make the cut
Telangana also had three institutions in the IIRF rankings for dental colleges. Army College of Dental Sciences, Secunderabad, was the highest-ranked Telangana institution at 33rd position. It was followed by Malla Reddy Institute of Dental Sciences, Hyderabad, at 53rd and Malla Reddy Dental College for Women, Hyderabad, at 64th.
Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences, New Delhi, secured the first position in the dental category.
What does IIRF measure?
The IIRF rankings are based on nine broad parameters, together accounting for 100% of the assessment. These include academic reputation; graduate outcomes and employability; research outcomes; demand ratio and student profile; employer reputation and international outlook; wellbeing and institutional development; peer perception and alumni feedback; public perception and data verification; and impact and value addition.
The methodology is intended to assess institutions beyond academic performance alone, taking into account factors such as research, employability, institutional development, stakeholder perception and the broader impact of an institution.

Walmart did ban Darling from its stores, as confirmed by a company spokesperson.
Darling was not banned for buying other people's groceries, according to the company — he recorded pranks and stunts in Walmart stores, which the company deemed disruptive enough for a ban. Furthermore, a video uploaded to Darling's YouTube page in April 2025 suggests he was banned from Walmart more than a year before this claim spread.
On Aug. 11, 2026, the social media influencer and comedian Damon Darling posted a video (archived) showing an interaction with a police officer telling him he had been issued a lifetime ban from entering Walmart stores. Darling has filmed many of his videos on Walmart premises, including a series in which he pays for other shoppers' groceries or gives out money.
As the video spread on social media, other users suggested that Darling had been banned specifically because he was attempting to pay for other customers.
Snopes readers contacted us asking for more information.
We found that the claim was a mixture of true and false information. Walmart confirmed it had banned Darling from its stores. However, according to the company's statement, he was not banned for his charitable actions.
We contacted Walmart and Darling's team for this story. We spoke briefly with a Walmart spokesperson via phone and received a statement via email, but had not heard back from Darling. We will update this story if we do.
Walmart's emailed statement to Snopes read:
Helping people is part of who we are, and we are always looking at ways we can partner with others to better our communities. Over the last two years, Mr. Darling repeatedly engaged in ways that created safety concerns and customer disruptions. We have a responsibility to create a safe and respectful place to shop and work, and will continue to do so.
Snopes found that while Darling's recent content may be more wholesome in nature, some of his older videos involved pranks and skits inside Walmart stores that shoppers may have complained about. Those older videos are not available on Instagram and other short-form video platforms but are still accessible on YouTube.
For example, in a video uploaded in February 2025 titled "Walmart Shoppers Do Anything For Money," Darling asks a woman to clip one of his toenails for $100. (Interestingly, Darling is never at a Walmart during that video — he's at a Kroger.)
Reviewing Darling's YouTube page also revealed that his ban may not have been as recent as people presumed. In a very brief clip at the end of a video uploaded on April 11, 2025, titled "Walmart BANNED me for life," Darling is approached by two police officers at a Walmart in Xenia, Ohio, who inform him that he has a trespass order for "all Walmarts."
While Darling and his team did not reply to Snopes' request for comment, the content creator did discuss the ban in an Aug. 11, 2026, interview with TMZ.
"I respect their wishes. I'm at a point where I'm just going to do what they ask me and not come back and not film at their business," he said. "I don't want any problems, I don't want anyone boycotting Walmart."

Australia’s first case of the deadly H5 bird flu in a little penguin has been confirmed on Victoria’s Phillip Island, only days after the state government announced it would begin vaccinating the species.
Confirmation of the virus in the little penguin will spark a race to vaccinate thousands of birds, with the government announcing on Saturday it would begin the rollout on Monday.
The government did not provide the exact location where the bird was found, but said it was not inside the island’s famous penguin parade area.
A spokesperson confirmed the little penguin had died.
There are about 40,000 little penguins on Phillip Island, making it the world’s biggest colony of the species and a major tourist attraction.
Environment advocates have been concerned about the potential for mass deaths of little penguins if the virus reached the island.
Euan Ritchie, a professor in wildlife ecology and conservation at Deakin university, said the detection of H5 bird flu in the much-loved little penguin population was “devastating”.
“Phillip Island is home to a diverse array and significant populations of native wildlife, including Australian fur seals, eastern barred bandicoots, and recently reintroduced bush stone curlews,” he said.
“Governments must provide whatever resources are needed to help wildlife survive through and recover from this bird flu outbreak.”
On Wednesday, the Victorian government announced plans for the world’s largest H5 bird flu vaccination program of wild birds.
The government said it would vaccinate up to 5,000 little penguins across populations at Phillip Island and at Melbourne’s St Kilda beach. While vaccinating wild birds is challenging, it was considered possible in Victoria’s wild little penguins because they generally return to the same burrows at Phillip Island and St Kilda each night.
But vaccination requires the delivery of two doses with a gap of a few weeks between each dose.
The detection on Phillip Island will spark concern that it may be too late for some little penguins to develop immunity.
Victoria’s chief biodiversity officer, James Todd, said he understood Victorians would be worried about the detection of the deadly virus in a little penguin.
“We know that the detection in a little penguin on Phillip Island is of concern,” he said.
“But we are proceeding with vaccination of the little penguin colony on Phillip Island and at St Kilda as a meaningful way in which it can help mitigate the impact of H5 on those populations.
“We know that little penguins are iconic and highly valued by Victorians, and for that reason, we are working as a priority to protect those colonies.”
The state’s chief veterinary officer, Dr Graeme Cooke, said Agriculture Victoria and Phillip Island Nature Parks “activated plans” to vaccinate little penguins as soon as the federal government authorised the vaccines for priority native bird species.
“Agriculture Victoria is working closely with Phillip Island Nature Parks to support vaccination of little penguins from Monday,” he said.
“While the first detection in a little penguin is a concern, vaccination of little penguins on Phillip Island remains a meaningful way to help protect this important colony.”
The Victorian government said there had been two further detections of H5 in greater crested terns, one at Lakes Entrance and the other at Dromana on the Mornington peninsula.
Todd said the Lakes Entrance detection was significant because it showed the virus was continuing to move through wild bird populations across Victoria.
On Saturday, the NSW government also confirmed the fifth detected case in the state, in a tern found at Eden on the far south coast.
The government said it would increase surveillance in the area as a result.
There have been two other confirmed cases in local birds in the state, one at Narooma on the state’s south coast and one at Wentworth in the far south-west. All of the confirmed cases in local birds have been in greater crested terns.

Alex Harman was on the last stretch of his trek to the top of Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania when he stopped on a steep part of the mountain. He had gone to bed at 3 p.m. the day before and set his alarm for midnight to start hiking early.
Now the sun was coming up, so he stopped to have a snack and take in the view, alongside around 30 of his McKinsey colleagues, before continuing on to the summit.
"The top was great," he said, "but that moment there where we all stopped and just watched the sunrise was very cool."
Harman, an AI product manager at McKinsey based in London, co-founded Mind Over Mountains, an employee-run initiative that gathers colleagues from around the world for a multi-day backpacking trip while raising money for charity.
It started with the Kilimanjaro trip in 2023 and continued with about 65 colleagues on a trek through Patagonia in 2025. This year, 100 McKinsey employees are heading to the Peaks of the Balkans in September for an eight-day hike spanning about 62 miles, or 100 km, all coinciding with the elite management consulting firm's 100-year anniversary.
The trips bring together McKinsey colleagues of all ages, experience levels, and roles, ranging from senior partners to entry-level analysts. Anyone from the firm's 40,000-person workforce can sign up. They are not official McKinsey retreats.
Employees organize them with the help of hired tour vendors and pay the full cost to attend. The Balkans trip will cost each attendee about $1,000, excluding airfare. No prior backpacking experience is required, and spots are available on a first-come, first-served basis, with demand growing each year.
"We filled 100 spaces in three hours," Harman said of the coming Balkans trip, adding they were "pretty blown away by the participation" and had to create a long waitlist.
For participants, the appeal is not just the destination. They described the treks as a rare chance to fully disconnect from work, spend hours with colleagues they might otherwise know only through Zoom or email, and temporarily leave office dynamics behind.
Seniority doesn't matter on the trail
Coordinating a backpacking trip for 100 people is no small task. Harman said a great deal of work goes into vetting and hiring local guides and vendors, adding he felt a "great deal of pressure" planning the Balkans trip. Organizing a weekend for friends is one thing, he said, but if you plan a trip for 100 McKinsey employees, "they'll notice everything, and they'll want it a certain way."
While on the trip, the days typically consist of breakfast, hiking — which includes some solo time as well as walking and talking with someone new — and a group dinner at the campsite.
"When you first walk next to someone, you have no idea what they do," Ting Cui, a principal product manager in London who went on the Patagonia trip, told Business Insider. "There's no way to know if they're a partner or if they're a business analyst. And obviously on the trail, it doesn't really matter where your seniority is."
Cui, who is also going to the Balkans, said she went into Patagonia not knowing the vast majority of the people on the trip, but that everyone gelled smoothly, which she thinks is a tribute to McKinsey's culture across its offices. She went away from the trip with lasting friendships. One colleague in New York who she bonded with on the trip ended up spending Christmas with her family.
Ricardo Moya Quiroga, a partner and COO counselor in McKinsey's Berlin office, also went on the Patagonia hike last year and is heading to the Balkans in September. He said he initially signed up to bond with McKinsey colleagues, raise money for charity, and for a personal detox. He turned off his phone and took a break from work and emails for the full five days.
"I was asking myself who I am, and the answer that came is: 'I am a grandpa, I am a husband, and I am a son.' Very clearly. It came spontaneously," he said, describing a moment on the trip when he decided to write a letter to himself. Since returning, he said he's been much more conscious of how he spends his time and said it was one of his greatest takeaways from the experience, along with connecting with colleagues and raising money for charity.
The trips can be hard, but they're worth it
The trips can be physically challenging, and things don't always go exactly according to plan. In Patagonia, Cui said one participant hurt his ankle and was limping toward the end of the day, but colleagues who had only recently met him stepped up and helped him reach camp.
On the Kilimanjaro trek, one of Harman's cofounders unexpectedly got blisters in a pair of boots that he'd hiked in plenty of times before. He borrowed Harman's Crocs and hiked in them up steep and sketchy terrain for a couple of days before finally deciding to cut the top part of his hiking boots off, the part that was causing the blisters, and wear those for the rest of the way.
Harman said that while the hiking itself is rewarding, raising money for good causes and connecting with people at work on a different level make the trips worthwhile. For the 2025 Patagonia trip, the group raised over $115,000 for mental health charities and hopes to raise another six-figure sum this year.
He said planning the trips has also been rewarding from an entrepreneurial perspective, which to him means "go do some cool stuff that no one asked you to do." He hopes the trips continue, even if he leaves McKinsey, and thinks others who are interested should start something similar at their companies, too.
"There will always be a bunch of corporate red tape. There will always be people who are worried," he said, adding that as long as your company appreciates an entrepreneurial drive, anyone could do it.
"No one's going to ask you to go do this," he said. "So just go do it and see how it lands."

When Edward Warchocki speaks with you, he sounds like a regular guy. “Not super intelligent, but very emotional, very easy to make friends with,” says Bartosz Idzik, the person who created him. But when he doesn’t talk, it’s harder to forget what Warchocki really is: a 4-foot-tall humanoid robot that’s wandering the city streets of Poland.
Six months ago, Idzik and his friend Radosław Grzelaczyk had the idea of buying a humanoid robot from China. They named it “Edward Warchocki” after Grzelaczyk’s dog Eddie and the Polish word for growling, “warczeć,” but also because it sounds like a passable name for a Pole. The first few days they took Edward out, it couldn’t speak, and people were clearly scared of it. Then Idzik, a software developer, wired Edward to a large language model that made it capable of having live conversations in Polish.
“When he started to talk, people loved him. Without talking, it’s just a 40-kilogram machine,” Idzik says.
Edward soon made lots of friends. It visited the Polish parliament and talked to politicians, hiked up mountains and waded in the lake, and was jokingly arrested by the police. In April, a video of it chasing away wild boars in Warsaw, armed with a backpack and a Rolex, went viral worldwide. By now, Edward has over 1 million followers and 4 billion views across social media.
In 2026, you must have seen at least one of these humanoid influencers vibing around the world. There’s “Rizzbot,” which wears a cowboy hat and flirts with passersby on the streets of Austin; “Bart Robot,” which was breakdancing with Knicks fans in New York, celebrating the team’s historic championship; and the “Brickell Clanker,” which changed into different jerseys to party with World Cup fans after each game.
But unless you’ve been paying close attention, you probably haven’t realized these robots are all the same model: Unitree G1, one of the most available and affordable humanoid robots on the global market today, made by a Chinese company that’s leading the robotics industry. The G1 is about the size of a child, with a hollowed-out face with a ring of blue light and light-gray limbs made of aluminum. It’s going on America’s Got Talent, showing off kung fu, having boxing matches, parkouring, dancing at concerts, running with kids, cooking (but failing), streaming with Kai Cenat, begging for money, dating itself, being ordained as a monk in Japan and Korea, and praying at a mosque in Dubai.
An anonymous shitposter on X put it: “This clanker is lit as fuck!”
Unitree will go public on the Chinese stock market in about two weeks. Its financial disclosure tells how popular the company’s products are: Unlike most robot companies whose products are still being tested in labs, more than half of Unitree’s 2025 revenue came from delivering humanoid robots to real customers. It shipped 5,511 humanoids in 2025 at an average price of less than $25,000 each. And 43 percent of all sales came from outside China. The company also became profitable for the first time last year.
“We tested a lot of humanoids, and the G1 was the best for its purpose,” Idzik says. “We are used to China copying other countries, but from the perspective of humanoids, other people should copy China. ”
Despite its commercial success, the company and its robots are often the subject of intense doubts. Sure, they can perform clout-seeking, crowd-pleasing tasks, but can they hold down a traditional job contributing to the economy, like working on an assembly line or cleaning a house? When will Unitree G1 get a real job?
Buying It in the US
Jake Cooperstein, a 24-year-old who lives in Miami, says he was inspired by Edward and other accounts to create a humanoid influencer of his own. In January, he visited the warehouse of a robotics shop in New York and tested the Unitree G1 robot. He was impressed by how easy it was to operate. The next day, he secured an order and paid the deposit.
On Unitree’s website, a basic G1 robot is priced at $13,500, but that’s before any tariff, shipping, and taxes. A US distributor lists the robot at about $19,000 instead. Cooperstein was not satisfied with that, though. The most basic version doesn’t come with more sophisticated parts like dextrous hands and is prohibited from modification. He instead chose the U5 variation that’s designed for educational buyers. It has more parts and better customization but sits at the price of $66,000.
Cooperstein named his G1 robot the “Brickell Clanker,” after the downtown Miami neighborhood, and started taking it out in public to interact with people.
Brickell Clanker got its big break by attending the World Cup games after-parties this summer, changing into different jerseys for Argentina, Brazil, and the US. Today, Cooperstein makes money mostly by charging a fee to bring Brickell Clanker to influencer parties, nightclubs, and corporate events. Rates range from $800 to $1,200 an hour, depending on what the robot needs to do.
Cooperstein recently got another robot: a Unitree R1. At almost one-third the base price of the G1, this faster, lighter model is Unitree’s attempt to make humanoids even more affordable. He named the new robot the “Lil Clanker.”
It’s unclear whether he’ll be able to keep buying Unitree’s robots. In July, the US Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on new Chinese-made humanoid robots. The models that had cleared approvals—like Unitree G1 and R1—are theoretically still allowed, but no one knows for sure. What’s certain is that when Unitree releases its next generation of humanoid robots, it won’t be able to sell them to the US. Unitree didn’t respond to a request for comment.
Hardware and Software Limits
In Europe, Edward Warchocki faces fewer threats. Idzik says MERA Robotics, the company he cofounded with Grzelaczyk, now has a fleet of 20 humanoid robots, most of them Unitree G1. Every robot in Poland shares the personality of Edward, but they also have some in the Middle East and Southeast Asia operating as different influencers.
While the LLM can enable the robots to converse freely, when it comes to physical movement they’re still under a lot of constraints. Both Idzik and the Cooperstein say that when they bring the robots out now, they are teleoperating the robots most of the time. Theoretically, the Unitree G1 should be able to move around in the physical environment by itself, but they are worried of a malfunction possibly hurting a bystander, creating a safety hazard.
The G1 robot that Cooperstein got came with about 20 gestures and 15 dance moves built in. Beyond that, it takes some technical knowledge to program new movements. For example, he taught the Brickell Clanker to move its arms in a way that simulates the signature “Viking Row” gesture done by Norwegian soccer fans this year.
Cooperstein still remembers the first day he took Brickell Clanker to the World Cup fan festival. Hundreds of people, including the press, circled the humanoid and cheered it on as it danced. “Nobody knows that it's me controlling it. It seems like I'm blending in with the crowd. I'm just staring out and looking at everybody,” he says, “and I'm like, ‘holy shit, this is the future.’”

When I decided to take a last-minute ski trip, despite never having skied before, I went straight to Columbia. Was I shredding the slopes? Absolutely not, but at least I was warm, thanks to my Snowy Summit Insulated Jacket and Bugaboo II Pants. Here at WIRED, we’re fans of Columbia. The brand makes reliable, well-priced outdoor gear for skiing, hiking, hunting, or just a day at the beach. Plus, there’s almost always a deal to be found.
WIRED reviewer Chris Haslam loves the Columbia Konos Trillium ATR as a value all-around trail-running shoe for faster hikes, day trips, and mixed terrain excursions. The plush cushioning and 8-millimeter drop are ideal on packed dirt, gravel, and woodland paths. For hiking boots, he recommends the Tellurix Titanium OutDry, which are waterproof, offer serious traction on wet rock and mud, and are surprisingly lightweight at 1.6 pounds per pair.
With summer approaching, now’s the time to prepare for outings, and if you’re eyeing snow gear, the off-season is when prices hit their lowest. I’ve gathered the latest Columbia promo codes to sweeten the deal.

22 more bodies recovered in Zimbabwe ferry disaster, bringing death toll to 68, police say
Police say 18 children are among the nearly 70 people killed this week when an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
HARARE, Zimbabwe -- Eighteen children were among the nearly 70 people killed when an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe this week, police said Saturday after rescuers recovered more bodies.
The ferry capsized in strong waves Tuesday and police said 22 more bodies were recovered since then, bringing the death toll to 68.
The aging ferry was traveling from Kariba town to rural and fishing communities in the country's northwest, where roads are damaged and public transportation is scarce. Authorities have not said how many people were aboard or how many remain missing.
Estimates have put the number of passengers as high as 153, while authorities say the ferry’s capacity is 90. Zimbabwe’s disaster management agency has said 77 people were rescued.
Authorities initially said the number of children aboard was unknown because those below ticketing age were not included in passenger estimates. A police list released later showed that 16 of the child victims were aged 10 or younger, with the youngest just 1.
Kariba is the world’s largest human-made lake by volume, created by damming the mighty Zambezi River in the late 1950s and early 1960s. It stretches more than 200 kilometers (124 miles) and is up to 40 kilometers (25 miles) wide in places.
Zimbabwe and Zambia share the lake, with their border running through its middle.

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.
The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it went over during heavy winds.
Eighteen children were among the people killed, Zimbabwe’s police said, in what is believed to be the country’s deadliest such disaster.
Most of the passengers are believed to be villagers and fish traders who lived around the lake.
Officials said the vessel was authorised to carry 90 people but was packed with 114 adults, five crew members and an unspecified number of children.
Lt Col Joseph Muchechesi, commander of the boat regiment involved in the search operation, said: “So far today we have managed to take 22 bodies. We are confident that we will manage to retrieve all the bodies.”
The civil protection unit said on Wednesday that 77 people had been rescued.
Hundreds of people gathered at the district hospital in the lakeside town of Kariba to identify the bodies of their relatives and loved ones.
A public memorial service was held in Kariba, nearly 280km (175 miles) north-west of the capital Harare, on Thursday before the burials started.
Survivors said they pleaded with the ferry driver to turn back as the vessel had begun taking on water soon after departing.
Chance Siyamavhu, 45, told the Agence France-Presse: “Thank God that a wave pushed the sinking vessel and we managed to climb on top.
“When the boat capsized, most of the people scrambled to get the lifejackets but most of them did not even know how to use them.
“Most people could not make it.”
Lake Kariba is the world’s largest manmade lake by volume. It stretches more than 200km (124 miles) and is up to 40km (25 miles) wide in places.
It was created in the 1950s during British colonial rule, when the Zambezi River was dammed, displacing about 57,000 people.
In 2014, 26 people, 24 of them children, drowned in Zambia’s part of the lake, when the boat meant to transport them to independence day celebrations capsized.
On the Zimbabwean side, five passengers drowned in a 2021 incident.

One Nation senator Tyron Whitten has claimed parents supporting their children who identify as transgender are engaging in “child abuse”, telling a fringe YouTube show: “there’s male, there’s female, and then there’s mental illness”.
Guardian Australia has unearthed several incendiary comments from Whitten and fellow One Nation senators Pauline Hanson and her longtime lieutenant Malcolm Roberts, about transgender Australians.
“They’re saying you can cut your dick off and become a woman … That’s a complete distortion of science,” Roberts told a podcast in June.
Whitten filmed an interview at Parliament House in August 2025 with a YouTube page called “Billboard Battalion”. The host recounts overhearing a Parliament House attendant escorting a group of schoolchildren.
“She turned around and said to me ‘thanks very much for your patience’, and I said, ‘thanks very much for calling them boys and girls’… when I was a young bloke, I never ever thought that would be a thing,” the host said.
Whitten responded: “Neither did I. Look, there’s male, there’s female, and then there’s mental illness.”
“If you want to wear a dress, that’s fine. I don’t care. But they can’t keep saying ‘hey kids, that’s normal.’ Well, no, it’s not.
“You’re going to be a boy or you’re going to be a girl. And parents that are promoting this, I think that’s child abuse.”
The Australian Human Rights Commission cites statistics that “around 2-3% of young Australians aged 11 to 18 years identify as transgender or gender diverse.”
Referencing research from youth advocacy group Minus18, the AHRC said “9 in 10 LGBTQIA+ young people said they had faced bullying or violence because of who they are, leaving many feeling isolated and unsupported.”
The offices of Whitten, Hanson and One Nation’s head office were contacted for response but did not respond to inquiries.
Roberts, whose previous comments on fringe podcasts about immigration and conspiracy theories have drawn controversy, in June was dismissive of transgender Australians in a YouTube interview.
Discussing problems he saw in Australia, Roberts said: “If you cut off your dick … you’re not a woman. [But] that’s now ingrained in law in Australia that you are.
“Not as crudely as that, but it just says that if you want to identify as a male, if you want to identify as a female and you’re a male, that’s your choice.”
In a March 2024 interview with former television host and AFL identity Sam Newman, Hanson – listing a number of her political concerns – mentioned “this transgender crap that’s going on, it frustrates me.”
“We’re allowing children under the age of 18 to have lifechanging operations that destroy their lives, ending up like vegetables, just destroyed, locked away in their bedrooms.”
However, the AHRC advises: “It is not legal in Australia to perform most gender-affirming surgeries on people under 18 years in the public health system.
“The only surgery allowed is breast reduction surgery for trans men, and only in very extreme circumstances,” it said in a fact sheet on transgender issues.
Parental consent and professional assessment is generally required for children to receive gender-affirming care, including hormone treatment or “puberty blockers”. Otherwise, a court order is required.
Equality Australia CEO, Anna Brown, said Australian law had “recognised trans people and their rights for decades.”
“Targeting one of Australia’s smallest and most marginalised communities isn’t just unfair, it fuels division, creates confusion and causes real harm. Trans people make up less than 1% of the population, yet they are being forced to carry the weight of a divisive and incredibly cruel culture war,” she said.
“This is a community that already experiences disproportionately high rates of discrimination, violence and exclusion. It’s clear some politicians are taking advantage of a lack of familiarity with trans people to manufacture fear and division, because turning minorities into political targets is an easy way to generate attention and relevance.”
The ABC reported on Wednesday the comments of Parminder Singh, who was third on One Nation’s ticket for the legislative council at the 2025 WA state election. Asked in a YouTube interview whether he thought people were born gay, Singh replied: “No, it’s a mental illness”.
Hanson on Thursday distanced herself from his comments, saying: “He’s not standing for One Nation … they’re not my views.”
Barnaby Joyce said on Wednesday, speaking to the ABC: “I don’t concur with [Singh’s] views.” He also defended One Nation’s record on LGBTI issues, saying: “I think you should get [One Nation party director] James Ashby on the show and ask him, he’s gay.”
“I think we’re one of the gayest parties in Australia,” he added.

Justin Blinder lost his job two weeks before the Covid-19 pandemic hit in 2020. To pay his rent, he turned to delivery services, riding his bicycle across New York City to deliver food. As he went, he noticed the disparities in where the food items went. Which order of Nomé sushi went where and how much people tipped.
“The city started to feel much more economically and psychologically disparate,” Blinder tells WIRED. “It really changed so much on a block-by-block level. These inequalities and demographic differences were happening in such close proximity.”
That experience has morphed into an art-project gadget called Ground Truth that Blinder hopes will raise awareness about the housing affordability crisis in New York City and beyond by making a Citi Bike—one of the ever-present ebike rental options across the city—harder to ride through places where it’s harder to live.
Blinder, a Brooklyn artist and contractor at Meta, received a $10,000 grant for the project from a Brooklyn arts organization called Idle Hands.
Ground Truth is a box that will trigger the brakes on the Lyft-owned bicycle, adding more resistance to the pedals when riding through rent-burdened neighborhoods, where people living in those areas spend more than 30 percent of their income on rent. Ride past an economically well-off block, and the bike is easier to pedal. Going past a block where rent takes the bulk of the households’ incomes can slow the bike down to a crawl.
There are two versions, one that can work on a regular bicycle and one built specifically for Citi Bikes.
The box mounts on the bike’s fork and is then attached to the front brake line. A battery-powered GPS component tracks the bike’s location. As it moves, the location is cross-referenced with household economic data from the US Census Bureau’s American Community Survey, stored on the device. When the bike passes a block the dataset says has a higher percentage of rent insecurity, the microcontroller triggers a small motor that applies the brake to add resistance, and the bike gets physically harder to pedal.
Blinder is also the creator of the Covid-inspired Pandemic Pulse, an app that used real time Covid statistics to change the brightness of your device’s screen. The screen would darken whenever data showed infections growing, and then black out briefly whenever a death was recorded. As with Ground Truth, Blinder says the goal of these projects is to help people understand large datasets in a more tactile way.
“It’s really trying to make the way we traditionally visualize a lot of big data more tangible and embodied,” he says. “Create something a bit more confrontational and try to force people to consider how they traditionally look at data.”
Blinder says the device is not a working product or something other people will be able to use. (Likely for legal reasons, as you can’t just change how a rideshare electric bicycle drives.) But he has ridden about 35 miles or so, filming the experience as Ground Truth changes its resistance in different communities.
He hopes the project will also call attention to the rising cost of renting a Citi Bike. The service has raised its prices for the past five years in a row.
“The price has just become so astronomical that it felt like this really nice connective tissue in the affordability crisis, connecting all of those different elements,” Blinder says. “It’s really thinking about how affordability changes throughout the city on a block-by-block basis and how this system could allow people to experience that.”

Jharkhand student protests began on 25 July 2026 over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC Preliminary and JSSC-CGL examinations, including allegations of OMR tampering. Led by student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, protesters have demanded cancellation of the exams and an independent CBI probe. On 10 August 2026, thousands of students marched towards the Jharkhand Assembly, where police used lathi charges and water cannons. The government has since agreed to cancel three JPSC examinations, but students continue to demand a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities. As of 14 August 2026, the protests have entered their 21st day, with Mahto continuing his hunger strike and political support for the movement growing (here, here, here, and here).
Amid this, a video is being shared on social media (here, here) claiming to show Abhijeet Dipke arriving in Jharkhand and participating in the student protests. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reaching Jharkhand and participating in the student protests.
Fact: The viral video does not show Abhijeet Dipke participating in the Jharkhand student protests. It actually shows him attending a CJP demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on 6 June 2026. While Dipke has supported the Jharkhand protests, he had not travelled to Ranchi at the time of writing this article. A CJP delegation, however, visited Ranchi to support the students. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A Google keyword search found no reports confirming that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke travelled to Jharkhand or joined the student protests. Instead, multiple reports (here, here) stated that he expressed verbal support for the protests but did not physically join them, saying he did not want to hijack the movement led by Devendra Nath Mahto. We also found reports that a CJP delegation travelled to Ranchi to support students protesting the JPSC and JSSC examinations.
We then conducted a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video, which led us to an X post by Deccan Herald dated 06 June 2026, featuring screenshots containing the same visuals as the viral video. The post was captioned, “‘We are not afraid’: CJP founder Deepak, who is leading the movement to remove Dharmendra Pradhan, has a message for the government.”
This photo was also used in a report published by Deccan Herald on 6 June 2026. According to the report, a crowd of students, young professionals, and activists gathered at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for a CJP demonstration led by CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, who had arrived from the United States earlier that day. The photo caption reads, “Founder of CJP during the protest”
Abhijeet Dipke reposted an X post by Jharkhand student protest leader Devendra Nath Mahato on 11 August 2026. The post mentioned a video call between Mahato and Dipke, during which Dipke expressed his support for the ongoing student protests in Ranchi.
To sum up, this viral video does not show CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reaching Jharkhand or participating in the student protests.

Family stranded at sea for 16 hours after jet ski capsized in Thailand

A French family was left stranded at sea for more than 16 hours overnight after their rented jet ski capsized off the coast of Thailand.
A 50-year-old father and his young sons were left "pale" and "exhausted after swallowing a lot of seawater" before being rescued, local government official Amorn Chomchoey told AFP.
All three were taken to hospital for checks but were discharged shortly afterwards, Chomchoey said.
The father had rented the jet ski for a 45-minute ride on Koh Samui, one of Thailand's most popular islands for tourists, at around 17:00 local time (10:00 GMT) on Thursday, the Bangkok Post reports.
Rescuers were alerted after the jet ski was not returned at the agreed time.
People used speedboats and more jet skis to comb the waters surrounding Koh Samui and towards the nearby island of Koh Phangan searching for the family, the Bangkok Post reports.
Search efforts had to be suspended overnight before the family were found still drifting at sea the following day, Thai media report.
The father and sons were found by rescuers at around 10:00 local time on Friday, according to AFP.
The father told authorities that rough waves had struck the jet ski and caused the engine to stop towards the end of the rental period, the Bangkok Post reports.
Footage of the rescue shows one of the boys sat on the top of the front of the jet ski while the rest of the vehicle is submerged beneath choppy waves.
His father can be seen waving at rescuers as he floats nearby. Both of them are wearing life jackets.
English-language news site Nation Thailand reports that the boys' mother and older sister had been waiting on the beach when the trio were brought back to safety.
The family has remained in Thailand and continued their holiday, officials told AFP.

French launch rescue operation as 140 migrants attempt Channel crossing to UK
Around 40 migrants got stranded by the tide as they waited to board a ‘taxi-boat’ off the coast of France
Around 140 migrants attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK were picked up by a French maritime rescue operation in the early hours of Saturday morning.
The complex operation, which deployed a number of rescue boats, began on Friday morning when the monitoring station in Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer spotted a migrant boat heading towards Dieppe, a fishing port on the Normandy coast.
Two patrol boats were then used to track the vessel as it made its way up to the Pas de Calais, the French authorities said on Saturday.
Around 40 people were waiting in the water off the coast near Berck-sur-Mer for the “taxi-boat” late on Friday.
Lifeboats monitored them, fearing they would be stranded by the tide, the maritime prefecture explained. And when they did become stranded, they were taken to the beach to be met by the fire and rescue service.
The boat then resumed its northward journey at around 1am, and reached another beach where 82 people were wearing life-jackets waiting to board.
At this time, there were around 20 people already on board the small boat, the prefecture said. Those waiting for the dinghy decided against boarding due to bad weather, and were again met by French rescuers back on land.
Eventually, those on board abandoned their attempt to cross at around 3.30am.
One child received medical attention for hypothermia. In a statement on Saturday, the French maritime prefecture said: “Determined to reach the United Kingdom, migrants attempting the crossing in precarious boats refuse assistance offered by French resources, accepting it only in cases of extreme emergency.
“Given the inherent fragility of these systematically overcrowded vessels, the decision is made not to force migrants onto state rescue ships, thus avoiding endangering lives in the event of a shipwreck.
“The maritime prefecture for the English Channel and the North Sea warns anyone considering crossing the Channel about the risks involved.”
Small boats used by migrants to make the journey across the Channel have been getting increasingly overcrowded. A record 230 people arrived to the UK in a single boat on Monday.
The inflatable boat was seen “buckling” in the water and could have led to a tragedy, according to French rescuers. The French lifeboat crew based at Berck-sur-Mer said the dinghy was 15m (49ft) long and was already carrying around 50 passengers when it was spotted heading towards a beach to pick up more.
French rescuers said that around 30 people ended up in the water during the rush to climb aboard the vessel at 5pm last Sunday, and had to be rescued.
The dinghy then headed towards the UK and was “buckling under the swell”.

Japan PM says Putin's visit to disputed islands 'absolutely unacceptable'
- Published
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has criticised Vladimir Putin's first-ever visit to the disputed Kuril islands on Thursday as "absolutely unacceptable".
Russian state media reported that Putin visited Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu, one of four islands in the Kuril chain that are claimed by Russia and Japan.
Putin's trip "has worsened Japanese sentiment towards Russia," Takaichi told reporters, maintaining the island chain was "a unique territory of [Japan] historically and under international law".
The countries have been locked in a dispute over the Kurils for decades, and it is the main reason Moscow and Tokyo did not sign a peace treaty after World War Two.
The Kuril islands sit between Hokkaido in northern Japan and Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. Four of the southernmost islands are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.
They are administered by Russia. At the end of World War Two, the Soviet Union annexed the island chain and deported around 17,000 Japanese residents.
During his visit, Putin sampled fish roe and spoke to island locals, Russian state media reported.
Speaking from the prime minister's office on Thursday, Takaichi said his trip "wounds the feelings of the Japanese people" and is "incompatible with Japan's consistent position on the Northern Territories".
"I hope that the Russian side will take the gravity of this matter very seriously," she said.
Earlier that day, Japan's foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi said the islands were "inherently Japanese territory both historically and under international law, and the Government of Japan strongly protests this visit".
Over the years, attempts to resolve the territorial dispute have made little progress. Bilateral ties have also remained frosty, with Japan imposing sanctions against Russia for its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Japan has protested against previous visits by Russian officials to the disputed islands, including Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and his predecessor Dmitry Medvedev.
The Kuril islands are a strategic area for Russia, which has beefed up its military presence on the islands over the past decade. The island of Iturup is used as its primary military air base in the region.
Last month, Chinese and Russian naval warships sailed through a strait in the Kuril islands during a joint patrol.
Russia also holds regular military drills near the islands, drawing condemnation from Japan.

The team manager for the Ugandan Commonwealth Games team has told BBC Scotland News he has no idea why four boxers with the team have vanished.

Media reports in Uganda, external suggested the four may be looking to seek asylum, but Uganda's chef de mission Godwin Kayangwe said he hoped the athletes would return home before their visas expire in October.

"I don't know anything about why they decided not to fly home but I know they communicated with their team manager and said they would be coming back.
"But after that their phones went off, so they have definitely broken the camp rules because no athlete is supposed to leave without permission.
"Their visas are still valid until October so hopefully, probably, they will come back to their country."
Asked why the athletes might be looking to seek asylum, the team manager said he didn't know.

He added that he had a simple message to the missing athletes.
"My message is pretty clear, observe the law and make sure the visa does not expire while you are still here. Come back to Uganda and and they can probably come back to Europe whenever they want."
