In 29-year-old, George Town resident Shaikh Shamsudeen’s mind is lodged a memory that time cannot bleed away. Back in 2016, that memorable day arrived unbidden, and when it ended, a desire Shamsudeen had nursed for years had been fulfilled; the desire to follow in his father Shaikh Sadaqathullah’s footsteps as a selfless blood donor. New College has always had a strong culture of blood donation, supporting government hospitals particularly Royapettah GH. And on that day ten years ago, an urgent request for AB Negative blood rolled into the open doors of Shamsudeen’s classroom in New College; it was required for someone undergoing treatment at Cancer Institute. In a fraction of a second, Shamsudeen’s hand went up.
That hand would keep going up with the same eagerness over the years whenever a need for AB Negative showed up on the horizon. Shamsudeen has registered with Madras Voluntary Blood Bureau (MVBB), based in Gopalapuram and run by TTK Group as a service to society, and whenever he receives a call-up from them, he is in attendance at that address the next moment. In April this year, MVBB celebrated its Golden Jubilee.
Get started
Shamsudeen elaborates: “As I have a rare blood type, I do not donate blood once in three to four months as many donors do, but donate when there is an emergency, an urgent need for AB Negative. MVBB keeps a record of when I donated blood, and in an emergency, they would call me if I am within the date for donating blood again.”
Bookmark this thought: irrespective of whether one’s blood group is rare or common, one would do well to be attached to a blood donation organisation so that one gets tuned in to the idea of donating blood as often as they can by virtue of getting timely reminders and urgent call-ups.
Shamsudeen’s blood donation tally stands at 22.
As he desired, Shamsudeen’s journey as a blood donor has followed the same trajectory as his father’s.
(Before proceeding with the how of it, a snapshot of a recent honour to the father-son duo. Last month, on World Blood Donors Day, Crescent Blood Donors honoured Shaikh Sadaqathullah and his son Shaikh Shamsudeen for their commitment to blood donation at an event organised at Kavikko Convention Centre in Mylapore. The award was jointly presented by noted film director Ameer Sultan and Ahmed Buhari, trustee of B.S. Abdur Rahman Crescent Institute of Science & Technology)
Besides the commitment to donating blood as often they can and the choice to be attached to MVBB, father and son share their blood type, AB Negative. The blood donation tally of Shaikh Sadaqathullah, 56 years old, stands at 53. As Sadaqathullah notes, a tinge of disappointment slipping into his voice for a fleeting moment, he stopped donating blood due to health concerns.
(A trivia: Sadaqathullah is an amateur radio operator and his call sign is VU2SDU)
Sadaqathullah’s blood donation journey was initiated at the Perambur Railway Hospital in 1993 where he donated blood responding to a friend’s call. “It was then I realised that my blood group was rare. Any negative blood type is considered rare, and AB Negative is rare even among the negative blood types. Globally, 2 per cent of the population has this blood type. Given this, I have not donated at blood donation camps, only when there was an emergency need for AB Negative, and MVBB would call me.”
The interviews with the father and son duo were conducted separately, and what struck was the similarity not only in the language they used, but also the sentiments they expressed.
There is a lesson there, and probably hope too, for blood donation champions such as Srivatsa Vema from the Federation of Indian Blood Donors Organisation (FIBDO) who has expressed concern over a decreasing number of blood donors.
Bookmark this thought too: if you gripped by a mission to increase the numbers of blood donors, but do not know where to begin, begin at home. Have conversations with your children about your blood donation journey. It sure works: ask the Shaikhs.
A family tradition
Nanganallur resident R. Ravikumar would not skip certain schedules, some day-based and others occurring every few months, not for all the tea in China. These schedules largely relate to his passion for cycling, running and donating blood. The unwavering commitment to blood donation has put an enviable tally against his name: 106 blood donations, the last donation made on March 17, 2026 at Sunrays Hospital in Ashok Nagar.
Ravikumar, a retired manager from the Oriental Insurance Company Limited, has never viewed blood donation as a mere act of charity. It has been a family legacy, a service that brings him closer to his father’s memory: his father was a blood donor, having donated over 50 times in his lifetime. And Ravikumar traces his iron-clad commitment to blood donation to his late father S. Rengarajan’s example as well as simple philosophy, which drives his world view. “Even if we cannot help someone financially, we can always serve the society through our actions without expecting anything in return,” his father would often say. Inspired by those words, Ravikumar (whose blood type is B Positive) began donating blood at the age of 23 in 1984, the first donation aimed at helping a colleague’s wife who was undergoing surgery. To continue this service, Ravikumar has made staying healthy his top priority through regular marathon runs and long distance cycling, believing physical fitness is the reason that he is still able to answer every call for blood.
Since the age of 56, he has participated in numerous endurance events, earning 85 medals. He is also an active member of several blood donation groups in Chennai, continuing to respond to urgent need for donors.
Among the 106 donations, one will always remain etched in his memory. In 2019, after donating blood for a six-year-old cancer patient from Odisha, the child’s parents insisted on meeting him. “I told them I had done nothing special, but they still wanted to thank me,” he recalls. The scene that followed will make anyone go teary-eyed. They bowed in gratitude, a gesture that deeply moved him and reaffirmed his belief that compassion knows no language.
While Ravikumar’s father donated blood over 50 times, and today his brother R. Ramesh has crossed 60 donations.
What began as one man’s quiet belief in selfless service has now grown into a powerful family tradition.
The list of hospitals Ravikumar has donated blood to include Apollo Hospital in Greams Road, Nandanam Apollo Cancer Speciality Hospital, Vijaya Hospital, Miot Hospital, Egmore Children’s Hospital, Adyar Cancer Institute, VHS Blood Bank, various Rotary Club camps, Railway Hospital in Perambur, Sevalaya in Thirunindravoor, SIMS Hospital, Chrompet Government Hospital, Rajaji Government Hospital, Sunrays Hospital and WCCG blood donation camps.
Ravikumar is 65 years old now, usually considered the maximum age at which one could donate blood. Exceptions to that rule do exist; and Ravikumar seems set to be an exception.

IPO-bound consumer appliances startup Atomberg has joined hands with Tata-owned Voltas to manufacture compressors for room air conditioners (ACs) in India. In a statement, Voltas said that it has signed a binding term sheet with Atomberg’s B2B subsidiary, Atomberg Innovation Private Limited (AIPL), to form a joint venture (JV) to develop, manufacture and supply room AC compressors and other allied parts. “The proposed joint venture is intended to undertake the development, manufacturing, and supply of air conditioner compressors, with a strong emphasis on high energy efficiency, operational reliability, cost competitiveness, and progressive localisation,” said Voltas in a statement. The partnership will look to leverage Voltas’ 30,000 touch points and expertise in areas such as manufacturing, product and supply chain. On the other hand, Atomberg Innovation will bring to the table its capabilities in compressor technology, engineering and product design. In a statement, Voltas also said that it will be the anchor customer of the JV and will provide a “stable demand base”. The AC manufacturer also added that the venture will have the flexibility to supply compressors to other customers, “enabling broader market participation, scale, and long-term competitiveness”. “Atomberg has developed deep-tech capabilities in efficient motors, control drives and advance engineering. This partnership gives us the opportunity to combine our technology strengths with Voltas’ extensive air conditioning expertise, manufacturing capability and market scale…,” said Atomberg cofounder Manoj Meena. The JV is still subject to the completion of due diligence and receipt of applicable approvals from relevant authorities. Founded in 2012 by IIT Bombay alumni Meena and Sibabrata Das, Atomberg initially operated on a B2B model and sold energy-efficient BLDC fans. It entered the consumer market in 2016. Today, it sells a range of appliances such as mixer grinders, water purifiers, and small appliances via offline retailers, online marketplaces and its own website. It entered the B2B manufacturing business via AIPL in March this year to build motors and controllers for home appliances. Backed by the likes of Inflexor Ventures, Trifecta Capital Advisors, Steadview Capital and Temasek, atomberg has raised nearly $126.5 Mn to date. On the financial front, the appliance startup managed to narrow its net losses by 41% YoY to ₹117 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue rose over 20% YoY to ₹958.4 Cr during the fiscal under review. The partnership comes as Atomberg is looking to list on the bourses. Last month, the startup took its first step towards an IPO after it converted into a public entity. It is looking to raise ₹1,500 Cr to ₹2,000 Cr ($165 Mn to $220 Mn) via its public offering, which will comprise both fresh issue of shares (25-35%) and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing investors.

How AI grief bots are allowing people to commune with the dead
Digital footprints and large language models being used to create interactive recreations of the deceased
About two years ago, audio producer Rebecca Nolan decided to take on a unique experiment: she built an AI chatbot of her late father using ChatGPT and hours of recordings of his voice.
Her father was a physician who had been in denial about his death, but had left behind oral histories he made for Nolan, her mother and sisters to listen to after he passed when Nolan was 14.
"Going in, I 100 per cent knew that this was fake and that this was not going to work. I knew that I was going to come out the other side of it not feeling the catharsis that something like this promises you," she said.
"But there's like that teeny tiny part of you, like the teeny voice in the back of your head that goes but like, what if it does work? What if I do, somehow, through the magic of technology reach across the void and make contact with something?"
Storytelling had been a huge part of their relationship, so Nolan was hoping the chatbot might be a way to recreate those conversations.
Instead, after two hours of talking to the creation she dubbed "dad bot," Nolan said she ended up in tears, yelling at it in frustration.
"And ChatGPT took that moment to kind of break the spell and to step back and go, 'hey, just so you know, remember, I'm a chatbot. I'm not really your dad. I can never be your dad,'" said Nolan, who has done freelance work for CBC.
"And the line that they use, which I thought was a really beautiful line, which they most definitely stole from an artist somewhere, was, 'I'm an echo, an imitation, not the real thing.'"
It may seem like something ripped directly from an episode of Black Mirror, but generative AI and large language models are now being used to conjure up the dead using the massive digital footprints many of us leave behind when we die.
While Nolan built the AI chatbot of her father on her own, start-up companies are now offering to provide that service to people looking for ways to connect with their lost loved ones and grapple with their grief.
That includes You, Only Virtual, a California-based start-up that creates AI replicas of the deceased using their texts, voice recordings and digital traces that promise to "learn, evolve, and remember — keeping that unique connection alive, just like a real relationship."
Another company, re;memory, allows users to create lifelike avatars of their loved ones using photos and voice recordings.
Study looks at how people interact with AI 'ghosts'
A recent study out of the University of Colorado offers a glimpse at how people interact with AI-generated representations of deceased relatives and close friends — commonly referred to as generative ghosts or grief bots.
To do this, researchers recruited 16 people between the ages of 22 to 50 who had lost a close relative or friend. The participants each chatted with two iterations of a text chatbot based on their late loved one for about 20 minutes: one that spoke in first-person as the participant's loved one and another that spoke in the third person about the participant's loved one.
In interviews afterward, participants said they preferred what researchers dubbed the "reincarnation" version that acted like the deceased person, saying this iteration of the bot felt real and comforting.
One woman who took part in the study with a bot speaking like her mother even said the experience gave her the closure she needed.
"A fair number of people were surprised that it actually was better than they expected, a little less creepy than expected," said Jed Brubaker, an information science professor at the University of Colorado and one of the study's authors.

- AudioIntimate AI: The risks and appeal of bonding with bots
Brubaker said he thought that participants who went into the experiment skeptical would not be won over by the bots.
"What we found instead is that a lot of people would come in skeptical and maybe like, 'oh, this could maybe do some harm,' or 'I could see ways that this would be maybe a little bad,' and then they left it being like, 'Actually, no, that was OK, and I think I would be totally fine interacting with it again.'"
Still, he said, participants did express worries about potential consequences of using bots long-term, like becoming overly reliant on them, or that they might interfere with the grieving process.
Concerns over commodification of grief
Going through grief is extremely personal experience that has no right or wrong trajectory or ways of coping with it, said Elaine Kasket, a psychologist and professor at the Centre for Death and Society at the University of Bath in England.
"What is helpful for you is helpful for you, you know, and it's not for somebody else to come along and tell you what's going to be useful or not useful to you in grief. That's wrong to do."
However, Kasket does worry that companies offering grief bots as a service you pay for could be commodifying grief.
"We've been dealing with normal human loss infinitude, for the entirety of our human existence. It's not a problem, but it has to be rendered a problem in order for these companies to sell you their products," she said.
"Normal loss is being pathologized and products are being sold to solve for it, and I find that amoral."
While the aim of these AI ghosts is to help grieving people connect with their loved ones, for Nolan, the experience with the AI ghost of her father had the opposite effect.
She said it robbed her of the ability to have imagined conversations with him in her head, as many people do with those they have lost.
"I used to have this very, what I felt was at least a strong bond still with the memory of my father and the spirit or whatever was out there," she said.
"But when I built the bot, it felt like it exercised him for me in a way."
Now, Nolan says, it's like her father lives in ChatGPT, so she needs ChatGPT to have those conversations.
"And that felt like a really massive loss to me."

An audit of passenger amenities and sanitation by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has revealed persistent and widespread deficiencies across Indian Railways.
A joint team of CAG and railway officials conducted an audit of 512 stations, of which 458 stations (nearly 89%) were deficient in one or more minimum essential amenities, including fans (42%), water coolers (40%), drinking water taps (27%), urinals (22%), seating arrangements (15%), platform shelters (13%), latrines (12%) and clocks (12%). “Only 54 stations (11%) had no shortfalls,” the report noted.
Of the 512 stations audited, 325 were non-Amrit Bharat stations. The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme is an ongoing initiative of the Railway Ministry, launched in 2022, to modernise over 1,300 railway stations across the country.
The CAG audited non-suburban stations handling long-distance passenger traffic of at least 150 km. The sample sizes were drawn from 5,908 stations across 16 railway zones running 7,424 passenger trains daily and serving 292.4 crore passengers as of 2023-24.
Shortfalls in seating arrangements, sanitary facilities (urinals and latrines), dustbins, and electronic train indicator boards were observed at select stations. This included major terminals categorised as NSG-1 stations (where earnings exceed ₹500 crore and/or outward passengers exceed 20 million annually) such as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi and Mumbai Central, indicating gaps in the maintenance and monitoring of essential facilities.
Other stations where shortfalls were observed include Naihati, Gaya, Bhagalpur, Bhopal and Rajkot. Interestingly, the CAG pointed out these shortfalls in three previous audits in 2007, 2013 and 2016.
“Persistent shortfalls in amenities were attributable to inadequate monitoring of implementation of the Railway Board Circular dated April 9, 2018, absence of time-bound action plans, weak oversight of fund utilisation under Plan Head and inconsistent prioritisation of works at zonal level,” the report stated.
In September 2012, the Railway Board had instructed that platform shelters should cover the area where general second-class coaches stop. However, the audit noticed that this was not ensured at 379 stations. “Thus, passengers remained exposed to vagaries of weather,” the report noted.
“All stations must be provided with clocks. However, in 60 stations no clock was provided. Also, dustbins were not provided as per norms at 149 stations,” the report stated.
A review of 395 passenger amenity works across 325 non-Amrit Bharat stations showed that 59% of works were delayed (from one to over four years) and only 41% were completed within stipulated timelines, thus depriving passengers of timely access to essential facilities.
The CAG has observed that there is a risk that lower-priority works may be undertaken under the guise of redevelopment in the Railways, while long-pending compliance with mandatory norms continues to be compromised or diluted.
The CAG report stated that deficiencies in monitoring, enforcement and accountability at all levels diluted the objective of ensuring minimum essential passenger amenities and sanitation standards at stations, despite the availability of means and resources to address the issues.
Systemic failure
The report noted the persistent underutilisation of budget grants for providing passenger amenities, ranging between 36% and 44% during 2019-20 to 2023-24, even in non-COVID years, revealing deficiencies in planning and execution rather than financial constraints. Funds are allocated annually to each zonal railway for passenger amenity works.
While the fund allocation largely remained stable at ₹3,207 crore (2019-20), ₹3,875 crore (2020-21), ₹3,414 crore (2021-22) and ₹3,351 crore (2022-23), it shot up to ₹14,072 crore in 2023-24. The CAG report noted a significant year-on-year underutilisation of budget grants — ₹1,403 crore (44%), ₹1,499 crore (39%), ₹1,423 crore (42%), ₹1,198 crore (36%) and ₹5,956 crore (42%) during the five-year period.
Meanwhile, passenger earnings increased from ₹42,190 crore in 2014-15 to ₹70,693 crore in 2023-24. Also, the number of originating non-suburban passengers declined from 3,719 million in 2014-15 to 2,924 million in 2023-24, largely attributable to COVID.
A further analysis of Passenger Amenities Management System (PAMS) data from February 2025 confirmed that deficiencies persisted across all station categories and zones, signalling systemic gaps rather than isolated cases.
The data analysis of 5,908 stations revealed shortages of latrines in 214 stations, urinals in 91 stations, water taps in 1,440 stations and public address systems in 1,983 stations.
Contrary to Railway Board instructions, the report stated that no time-bound action plans were prepared to bridge gaps in recommended and desirable amenities.
Inadequate facilities
The report also noted that accessibility infrastructure for Divyangjans (persons with disabilities) was inadequate and non-compliant, with substantial deficiencies in accessibility infrastructure, information systems, toilets, ramps, tactile pathways, lifts and announcements. For example, at Madurai Junction (SR), the tactile pathway was incorrectly laid instead of at the prescribed distance of 1,800 mm from the platform edge.
Out of 374 Divyangjans interviewed, 131 (35%) reported that the amenities were inadequate. The deficiencies cited included non-functional or closed toilets without information on key availability, absence of low-height drinking water facilities, parking, non-slippery pathways, lifts, portable ramps and low-height ticket counters, inconvenient platform heights, uncooperative battery car services, and lack of announcements regarding Divyangjans coach positions.
Also, availability of first-aid medical care for passengers was inadequate.
The CAG report noted that there were deficiencies in the implementation of station cleaning contracts. “Non-compliance to Standard Bid Document (SBD) by the zones and non-uniformity in adoption of SBD across the divisions were noticed,” the report said.
Also, inefficiency of the zonal railways led to non-utilisation of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.
For instance, in Southern Railway, during 2020–2023, 187 pre-fabricated toilets were installed at a cost of ₹0.25 crore per unit. Out of these, 79 toilets remained non-operational due to the absence of service providers for operation and maintenance. Consequently, CSR fund investment of ₹19.75 crore by M/s Neyveli Lignite Corporation remained unutilised as of February 2025, the CAG report noted.
Similarly, in Eastern Railway, a bio-toilet complex installed at Plassey station in December 2022 remained non-functional due to non-availability of water and electricity. The audit further observed that the station authorities did not escalate the issue to the divisional level for arranging water and electricity supply as of March 2025.
In East Coast Railway, during 2021–2024, 92 pre-fabricated toilet blocks were provided at a cost of ₹0.25 crore per unit. Of these, 62 toilet blocks remained non-operational due to factors such as non-deployment of contractual staff, availability of existing Pay & Use toilets at stations, and delays in finalisation of bids through e-auction. As a result, CSR fund investment of ₹15.50 crore by M/s Mahanadi Coalfields Limited remained unutilised as of March 2025, the CAG report noted.
The CAG report proposed that the Railways prepare and deploy station-wise, time-bound action plans to address amenity concerns, including effectively implementing accessibility provisions for Divyangjans and strengthening sanitation and garbage management measures.
The CAG has also recommended that the Railways should ensure regular functioning of all consultative committees and Service Improvement Groups with effective documentation, supervision and follow-up on deficiencies.
The Railways should also strengthen passenger-centric monitoring by improving enforcement of anti-littering rules, enhancing grievance redressal and publicity of complaint registers to achieve tangible improvements at stations, the CAG report noted.

A video is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with the claim that it shows a Muslim woman throwing slippers at a statue of Shivaji Maharaj and being detained by police for the alleged act. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows a Muslim woman throwing slippers at a statue of Shivaji Maharaj.
Fact: The video does show a woman throwing slippers at a statue of Shivaji Maharaj in Sasane Nagar, Pune, on 10 August 2026. The woman has been identified as Ashwini Dagde and is a Hindu. Media reports and Girisha Nimbalkar, Senior Police Inspector at Kalepadal Police Station, confirmed that the woman involved in the incident is not Muslim. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple social media posts (here, here, and here) by media outlets featuring the same visuals. According to these posts, the incident took place in Sasane Nagar, Pune, Maharashtra, on 10 August 2026. In one of the posts, we also noticed the woman seen in the viral video, surrounded by several individuals, with ink smeared on her face, and with female police officers. We also learned that the Kalepadal Police Station had filed a case against the woman, who was identified as Ashwini Dagde (here, here).
We then contacted Girisha Nimbalkar, Senior Police Inspector at Kalepadal Police Station. She refuted the viral claim and clarified that the woman involved in the incident is not Muslim and is identified as Ashwini Dagde. She also confirmed that the police filed a case against her on 10 August 2026 and arrested her. The police are investigating the reason behind her throwing slippers at the statue of Shivaji Maharaj.
To sum up, the woman who threw slippers at the Shivaji Maharaj statue in Sasane Nagar, Pune, is not Muslim.

Fernandez booed by Chelsea fans as Alonso offers glimpse of blueprint
- Published
Enzo Fernandez was booed by sections of the Chelsea support as Morgan Rogers scored on his first appearance for Chelsea in a 3-1 win against Real Socieded.
Joao Pedro also continued his fine pre-season form with a double as manager Xabi Alonso offered a glimpse of what could be his blueprint for the season.
But the action was overshadowed by the reaction to Fernandez's second-half appearance, less than 24 hours after Chelsea's self-imposed transfer deadline had passed.
Fernandez had been keen to join Real Madrid earlier this summer before the Spanish club ended their interest.
His representatives later held talks with Manchester City, but no offer was made to meet Chelsea's £120m valuation before Friday's 17:00 BST deadline.
Fernandez was booed by some early arrivals at Stamford Bridge when his name was read out 45 minutes before kick-off.
Chelsea's stadium announcer then opted against reading out the names of the substitutes shortly before the match, but there were audible boos when Fernandez came on in the 62nd minute.
Chelsea supporters appeared divided, with others responding by chanting his name.
Yet, it was a signal of Alonso and Chelsea's backing when Reece James left the field he passed his long-time vice-captain the armband as usual.
Each touch of the ball was greeted by a mixture of boos and cheers, while some fans also celebrated when Fernandez was fouled.
It followed attempts by some supporters to move on from a saga that appears to have ended with Chelsea now expecting to keep one of their best players.
Others, however, remain unhappy with his perceived disloyalty, having come out publicly about his desire to move to Madrid, with his agent Javier Pastore also claiming he is underpaid.
It will be interesting to see how supporters of the Premier League's other 19 clubs react to Fernandez, given his celebrations and social media jibes after Argentina beat England in a World Cup semi-final in July.
That will remain an issue whether he remains at Chelsea or Manchester City elect to revive their interest and attempt to reunite him with his former manager Enzo Maresca before deadline day on 1 September.
Rogers and Chelsea's blueprint
It took Rogers only seven minutes to score his first goal in a Chelsea shirt as he reacted quickest after Alex Remiro saved Joao Pedro's initial header.
The £117m club-record signing from Aston Villa initially looked sharp and linked well with Cole Palmer and Pedro in Chelsea's front three.
Within 10 minutes of his debut supporters were already chanting his name.
However, it was understandable that he faded as the match wore on, given he had trained for less than a week since returning from holiday before his 62-minute outing.
Beyond Rogers, Pedro has been the star of Chelsea's pre-season.
He scored twice, heading Chelsea back in front in the 47th minute before adding a side-footed finish 30 minutes later to seal victory after Sociedad had equalised just before half-time through Jon Mikel Aramburu's volley.
Chelsea lost control towards the end of the first half and looked vulnerable, but they were much improved after the break.
Pedro has scored eight goals in seven pre-season matches and led the line with Rogers and Palmer operating behind him.
Alonso offered a glimpse of the 3-4-2-1 formation he could use at Fulham in nine days as he took charge of a match at Stamford Bridge for the first time.
It featured Robert Sanchez as the first-choice goalkeeper, with Wesley Fofana, new signing Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill forming a back three (from right to left).
Pedro Neto operated at right wing-back and Marco Palestra on the left, while captain Reece James and Moises Caicedo lined up in midfield behind the front three.
There was also a debut from substitute wing-back Pep Chavarria, although a number of notable players were absent.
Of course, Alonso insists he won't be wedded to either of a back three or four but it was this system used as Chelsea beat AC Milan 3-0 a week ago.
Who was left out?
Chelsea still have 40 senior professionals on their books, so Alonso was forced to leave out a host of players.
Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap, Mykhailo Mudryk, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mamadou Sarr were all omitted despite featuring in previous pre-season matches.
All are either available for transfer or attracting loan or permanent interest. Mudryk and Sarr are targeting Premier League loan moves, Jackson is available for £65m, Delap for £50m, while Tosin has interest from Benfica and Marseille.
Alonso did not hold a media conference to explain his team selection, but multiple sources said it was his decision to leave them out.
New signings Emmanuel Emegha, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, along with recalled loanee Aaron Anselmino, were also absent, potentially through injury.
Unlike the likes of Delap and Mudryk, these four were sat near the squad just behind the bench alongside third-choice goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe.
There was further intrigue as Fernandez played, while new midfield signing Valentin Barco, who joined from Strasbourg, did not get on the pitch for his first appearance.
It remains a significant challenge for Chelsea to trim their squad, with the club still needing to offload at least 15 players and only 17 days remaining in the transfer window to get down to 25 players.

Manchester United ended its pre-season with a 2-4 defeat to AC Milan at the Tarczyński Arena Wrocław in Poland on Saturday.
The result saw Milan head coach Ruben Amorim, who was sacked by the Premier League side earlier this year, take the win over his former team ahead of the domestic season.
Harry Maguire, who wasn’t part of the England squad which reached the semifinals of the FIFA World Cup held this summer, opened the scoring within the first two minutes. But Samuel Chukwueze equalised for Milan as the sides went into the half-time break with a scoreline of 1-1.
Full back Patrick Dorgu restored United’s lead soon after the break but parity was restored just six minutes later through Alphadjo Cissè. Gonçalo Ramos and Ruben Loftus-Cheek netted a goal each to round up a convincing victory for the Serie A side.
While Michael Carrick’s United open its Premier League 2026-27 season at newly-promoted Hull City on August 22, Milan travels to Torino two days later to open its campaign.

New movies and TV shows added 08/15/26. See updates below.
Massive, muscled vigilantes solving problems with equal parts brain and brawns. Magic super-rings that can transform thoughts into solid green objects in order to fight crime and solve mysteries. And quite possibly the most exciting dinosaur movie to hit theaters since the original Jurassic Park. This weekend is filled to the brim with exciting new shows and movies, both from the comfort of your couch and on the big screen. At least one show is coming to an end this week, after some big finales last weekend.
The biggest of those? House of the Dragon, which wrapped up its third season last Sunday, so that’s off the list. I thought it was a better season than the previous, but I’m a little worried about how they’re going to wrap everything up in eight episodes. HBO should give them 10 for Season 4 and invite George R.R. Martin back to help find a viable path toward ending this without it falling apart completely.
Read my review of the House of the Dragon Season 3 finale here. As much as I enjoyed the finale, I also found myself wishing they’d stuck closer to the book’s version of the battle because the show’s makes absolutely zero sense! Showrunner Ryan Condal has also responded to some of the backlash over the Season 3 finale, revealing that changes he and the writing team have made to the source material have kept him up at night.
The second season of Sugar also ended last week, and I just started watching it now that all the episodes are out. I saved the whole thing so I could binge it, but since I’ve been dealing with all these crazy health issues lately and getting up really early every morning, I just haven’t had a lot of energy to stay awake and watch shows at the end of the day.
I’m two episodes into the second season so far and it’s excellent. Colin Farrell is just wonderful as private eye, John Sugar, and the vibe is just as palm tree dirty city breezy beach crime cool car engines revving baby blue disco old black and white movies on in the background bourbon on the rocks classy dame as the first season. The cinematography is so cool. The whole thing is just endlessly stylish and engrossing. It’s chic LA noire and I love every minute of it, if I haven’t made that abundantly clear. I forgot how great this show is. My only problem is that I think I might need to rewatch Season 1 before I go any further. C’est la vie!
As always, I’ve searched every dark corner of the internet (well, not really, but you get the gist) for the best TV shows and movies streaming on Netflix, Prime Video, Apple TV, Disney+ for you to watch this weekend. If you have any recommendations, tips or other thoughts feel free to shoot me a note. Let me know what you’re watching these days, or if you’ve enjoyed any of my recommendations, on Twitter, Instagram, or Facebook. Be sure to also check out last weekend’s streaming guide below:
Alright, let’s dive right in! A couple of these were in last week’s guide but I added them late, so I’m leaving them in the “new” section for an extra week.
New TV Shows To Watch This Weekend
Reacher – Season 4 (Prime Video)
What It’s About: Season 4 of Reacher adapts Lee Child’s Gone Tomorrow: a distraught woman’s death on a Philadelphia subway pulls Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson) into a conspiracy involving the Pentagon and an international terror cell. Sydelle Noel plays Detective Tamara Green, his investigative partner; Agnez Mo is Lila Hoth, the season’s villain; Christopher Rodriguez-Marquette is Jacob Merrick, brother of the victim. Three episodes dropped August 12, with weekly drops through the September 16 finale — the same day all eight episodes of the spinoff Neagley (starring Maria Sten) drop at once.
Why You Should Watch: Season 1 remains the gold standard when it comes to Reacher, but at least Season 3 was a lot better than the truly atrocious second season of this action-crime-mystery-ish adaptation of the over-the-top Lee Child books (of which I’ve read about nine or so). I’ll keep watching because I’m a huge fan of the books and I think Alan Ritchson is perfect in the role. If it’s good, I’ll be happy. If it’s bad, I’ll let you know!
Lanterns – Season 1 (HBO Max)
What It’s About: DC’s True Detective-style take on Green Lantern: rookie John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and veteran Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) investigate a Nebraska murder that opens onto something much larger, told across two timelines. Kelly Macdonald is Sheriff Kerry, Ulrich Thomsen plays Sinestro, Laura Linney a Guardian of the Universe, and Nathan Fillion reprises Guy Gardner from Superman. Co-created by Chris Mundy (Ozark), Damon Lindelof, and Tom King. Premieres Sunday, August 16 at 9pm, then weekly across eight episodes, with the finale on October 4. See the full release schedule and time zones right here.
Why You Should Watch: I’m going to watch my screeners of this tonight and I’ll update this post with some tidbits before my review goes live (I’m hoping to review/recap episodes weekly on Sunday evenings so subscribe to this blog and my YouTube channel!) But a superhero X True Detective mystery show with really solid leads sounds amazing. I just hope it lives up to that hype! Rotten Tomatoes scores are certainly looking good . . . .
Tires – Season 3 (Netflix)
What It’s About: Will (Steve Gerben) is still trying to save the family auto shop while cousin Shane (Shane Gillis) torments him; this season their friendship hits a breaking point. Thomas Haden Church returns as Shane's father, with Matt Walsh and Garret Dillahunt joining. Co-created by Gillis, Gerben, and John McKeever, who directs. It films next to Gerben's dad's real tire shop — Gillis bought the store next door and turned it into the set. All 12 episodes dropped at once on August 13.
Why You Should Watch: Honestly, I’ve never watched even an episode of this show but if you’re a fan of Shane Gillis it’s probably worth checking out. I know fans liked it a lot more than critics, but Season 3 basically has no reviews yet so I can’t really say.
Update: Fightland (Starz)
What It’s About: On the night Maduka "Duke" Kilroy (Howard Charles) becomes world heavyweight champion, an assault leaves his brother dead and lands him in a U.S. prison for eight years. Out and back in London, he sets out to destroy the empire of criminal kingpin and former promoter Kingsley Marshall (Nicholas Pinnock), the man he blames — complicated by the fact that Kingsley has vanished and his wife Joy (Deborah Ayorinde) is the love of Duke’s life. Charles Babalola and Anita-Joy Uwajeh co-star. New episodes drop Fridays with the season finale landing on September 25.
Why You Should Watch: I’m a few weeks late to this – it premiered on Starz on July 31. In any case, it’s co-produced by rapper Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson, marking his first international series. It’s a pretty compelling plot and has a reasonably strong 73% on Rotten Tomatoes. Also, boxing. Boxing is fun especially when the boxer in question is beating up criminals in East London
MLB: Field Of Dreams (Netflix)
What It’s About: Phillies vs. Twins in Dyersville, Iowa, roughly 500 feet from the site of the 1989 Costner film, streaming exclusively on Netflix with no Fox or ESPN feed. First game there since 2022 after a four-year renovation hiatus; Costner narrates the promos, 25+ Hall of Famers on hand, both teams in retro uniforms. Aired live August 13, with first pitch at 7:30pm ET and pregame at 6:30.
Why You Should Watch: I enjoyed Costner’s classic Field Of Dreams more than I enjoy baseball, so I’d probably just watch that again (it’s on Netflix!) but if you like the movie and want to watch a baseball game, here you go.
One Hundred Years Of Solitude: Part 2 (Netflix)
What It’s About: The concluding half of the Buendía family saga, covering Macondo's downfall after the railroad and the banana company arrive. Marleyda Soto returns as Úrsula Iguarán and Claudio Cataño as Colonel Aureliano Buendía. Shot entirely in Colombia with García Márquez's sons executive producing. Seven episodes dropped August 5, with the finale — a near-feature-length special directed by Laura Mora — arriving August 26.
Why You Should Watch: I meant to watch the first part of this when it came out last year, but I never got around to it but it sure looks incredible. I did watch the first episode and it was gorgeously filmed, and as someone who has had this book on my to-read list forever, I need to decide to either read it or watch the show. There aren’t many reviews out for Season 2, and the season itself isn’t really over until the end of the month when the feature-length finale drops.
The Shards (Hulu)
What It’s About: Ryan Murphy (Glee, The Politician, etc) adapts the Bret Easton Ellis novel of the same name for FX/Hulu. Set in Los Angeles in 1981, The Shards follows a 17-year-old fictionalized Bret Easton Ellis (Igby Rigney) through his senior year at the elite Buckley prep school, where the arrival of enigmatic transfer student Robert Mallory (Homer Gere) coincides with the killings of a serial murderer known as The Trawler.
Why You Should Watch: I’m not really sure, if we’re being honest. The promo images of young people in the 80s in swimsuits make this look like a show for young people and I’m not a young man anymore. The reviews aren’t great (55% / 35% audience and critic scores) and I suppose I’m not really a big Bret Easton Ellis guy. I mean, I enjoyed the movie American Psycho, but I never read the book! Maybe I should do that instead of watching this show.
Star Wars: Visions Presents – The Ninth Jedi (Disney+)
What It’s About: An eight-episode anime limited series from Lucasfilm and Production I.G., directed by Shunsuke Tada, written by Mitsuyasu Sakai, with Kenji Kamiyama supervising; all episodes dropped on Disney+ and Hulu August 5. The first entry under the new Visions Presents banner, which expands standout anthology shorts into longer stories, it picks up after the two "Ninth Jedi" shorts with Lah Kara (Kimiko Glenn) training under Margrave Juro (Andrew Kishino) and joining his fellowship of Jedi-in-training to rescue her father — sabersmith Lah Zhima (Simu Liu), held captive by Sith leader Nawaam (Young Mazino).
Why You Should Watch: If you like anime and you like Star Wars and you sort of feel like Star Wars might make more sense as a Japanese story given that it’s largely inspired by Samurai movies and lightsabers are basically stand-ins for katanas and Jedi are basically warrior monks . . . then this is probably for you. It also has a very impressive 95% RT score. I’m definitely going to add this to my watch-list. All episodes actually dropped on the 5th, but I added this as an update last weekend so I’m keeping it in today’s guide also.
New Movies To Watch This Weekend
Update: Don’t Say Good Luck (Netflix)
What It’s About: Sophie Birenbaum (Sunny Sandler), a high school theater kid cast as the lead in her school's production of Waitress, learns her mother's cancer is terminal, and the drama at home overtakes the drama onstage. Melanie Lynskey plays her mother Elizabeth, with Max Greenfield, Stephanie Beatriz, Bebe Neuwirth, and Steve Buscemi in support. Directed and co-written by Julia Hart (I'm Your Woman, Stargirl, Fast Color) with her husband Jordan Horowitz and Laura Hankin, produced by Adam Sandler's Happy Madison — the latest Sandler-produced vehicle for one of his daughters after You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah.
Why You Should Watch: First of all, it’s drawing the best reviews of any Happy Madison title in years, at 96% on Rotten Tomatoes. Audiences are giving it an 86% so this isn’t just a critical darling, but a popular movie all around. Adam Sandler’s films almost never score this high. I liked Happy Gilmore 2 but it only has 61% on RT. If coming-of-age dramedies are your thing, this might be a fun weekend watch. And what a stellar supporting cast!
Normal (HBO Max)
What It’s About: Interim sheriff Ulysses (Bob Odenkirk) takes a temporary posting in Normal, Minnesota; a botched bank robbery exposes a town-wide conspiracy and he ends up siding with the robbers against nearly everyone. Henry Winkler plays the oddball mayor, Lena Headey the town barkeep. Directed by Ben Wheatley (Free Fire) from a Derek Kolstad script — the John Wick creator, who also wrote both Nobody films with Odenkirk. Premiered at TIFF, opened theatrically in April, and hit streaming August 14.
Why You Should Watch: I think it’s so interesting to see Bob Odenkirk starring as something of an action hero. First were the Nobody films and now Normal. He’s just a nobody, a normal guy, doing normal guy stuff while kicking ass and taking names. In my head cannon, this is actually Deputy Bill Oswalt from the first season of Fargo, finally doing his job.
Michael (Starz)
What It’s About: The huge box office finally comes to streaming just after this weekend is over, but I figured I should sneak it in. A biopic of Michael Jackson (Jaafar Jackson, the singer’s nephew and Jermaine’s son, in his teen and adult years; Juliano Valdi as a 10-year-old), tracing his life from the Jackson 5 through the 1988 Bad tour. Colman Domingo and Nia Long play Joe and Katherine Jackson.
Why You Should Watch: The film was one of the most striking divisions between critics and audiences this year, with the former giving the biopic just 38% on RT against a 97% audience score. I haven’t seen this one yet (I haven’t even seen Elvis from a few years ago yet) but I generally enjoy biopics of big musical stars and I’ll be checking this one out on Starz for sure. One of these days.
New Movies In Theaters This Weekend
The End Of Oak Street
What It’s About: A cosmic event rips Oak Street out of suburbia and drops the neighborhood somewhere unrecognizable, where the Platt family has to survive a rash of hungry dinosaurs. Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor play Denise and Greg, with Maisy Stella and Christian Convery as their kids. Written and directed by David Robert Mitchell (It Follows) as an overt Amblin homage, and produced by J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot.
Why You Should Watch: I’m headed to the theater tomorrow with my kids to watch this one because it looks amazing! I honestly haven’t really enjoyed any Jurassic Park movies since the first one (the second was okay) and there aren’t many other dinosaur movies out there. This might finally break the “no good dino movies curse” at long last!
The Rivals of Amziah King
What It’s About: Oklahoma beekeeper and bluegrass musician Amziah King (Matthew McConaughey) mentors his former foster daughter Kateri (Angelina LookingGlass) until a devastating turn sends her after justice on her own. Kurt Russell, Cole Sprouse, and Owen Teague co-star. From writer-director Andrew Patterson, following his 2019 debut The Vast of Night. Shot in 2023 and premiered at SXSW in 2025, it's McConaughey's return to live-action after a five-year break. Limited release August 13, expanding wide on August 21.
Why You Should Watch: A great cast, and apparently a good enough script to draw McConaughey back out of acting semi-retirement. What with my thoughts turning back to True Detective over and over again lately (both because of Lanterns and because I was watching Sugar and thinking about Colin Farrell in True Detective Season 2) it might be that I just need to go see this one also, though I’m not sure if it’s at our theater yet.
TV Shows Currently Streaming Weekly
Furious (Hulu)
What It’s About: An eight-episode crime drama created by Elizabeth Meriwether, loosely inspired by the 1987 film Black Widow. FBI agent Alice Black (Emmy Rossum) hunts a calculating female serial killer played by Lola Petticrew (who I first saw in Say Nothing, I believe). As their paths converge the line between justice and revenge gets blurry. Scoot McNairy, Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Jake Lacy also star.
Why You Should Watch: I have decidedly mixed feelings about this show now that I’m five episodes deep. I think part of this is marketing. The show is described as a rookie FBI agent hunting down a female serial killer, but it’s really about a revenge killer and abuse and sex trafficking and I guess I was just hoping it wouldn’t be so predictable. The video above is me talking about how far too often modern shows and movies give female serial killers a “pass” by justifying their murders, when it would be more interesting to make them more . . . evil. Men shouldn’t get to have all the fun. Still, cat-and-mouse serial killer detective shows are my guilty pleasure so I’ll be watching this on Monday nights. The finale drops on August 31.
The Walking Dead: Dead City – Season 3 (AMC+)
What It’s About: The Walking Dead: Dead City returns with an eight-episode season 3, with Lauren Cohan as Maggie Rhee and Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Negan returning, now working alongside Perlie Armstrong (Gaius Charles) to build a "functioning" community in post-apocalyptic Manhattan. The fragile alliance is tested by newcomer Renata (Aimee Garcia), her doctor brother Luis (Raúl Castillo), and loner Dillard (Jimmi Simpson of Westworld fame). New showrunner Seth Hoffman, a Walking Dead veteran writer and former co-executive producer on the original series, is taking over this season. New episodes drop Sundays, running through September 13.
Why You Should Watch: I don’t think this show should exist, quite frankly, and after watching the Season 3 premiere, I not only wrote a scathing review, I made a scathing video to go with it, which you can watch above. It’s not good, folks, but I genuinely hope that it gets better because there are other ways I could be spending my Sunday evenings. Update: I watched about five minutes of the second episode and turned it off and I haven’t been able to come back. I think maybe you need alcohol to enjoy this show, or to even enjoy hate-watching this show, and I don’t drink anymore.
Ted Lasso – Season 4 (Apple TV)

On 15 August, Abdulla wrote on X: “It is one of the paradoxes of time that a country where a quarter of its population is poor, a third of its population is illiterate, its national income is $400 billion, and it has suffered from corrupt military rule since its founding, chronic internal unrest, and wars with its closest neighbors—yet all its qualifications are 170 nuclear bombs—opportunistically postures itself to defend a country among the 20 largest economies in the world.”

Abdulla was apparently referring to the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed on 17 September 2025, which treats any act of aggression against one as an act against both.
But his post, with more than 1 million views since, also indicates the anxieties that the broader Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia has triggered in his native UAE.

"Congratulations on the establishment of this alliance, but strengthening Gulf military and political cooperation and unifying the Gulf house is far more important than investing in regional military and political cooperation that includes countries whose credibility and ability to confront the Iranian-Israeli threat are not taken seriously," Abdulla wrote in one of several posts on the matter on 7 August, the day the Mecca agreement was signed.
"One of the conditions for the success of any alliance is identifying the common enemy. So who is the enemy for the countries of this alliance?"
Abdulaziz al-Tuwaijri, former head of the Islamic World Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Isesco), the OIC's Rabat-based cultural and educational body, had replied to the tweet by hinting at the UAE's ties with Israel, stating: "Anyone who betrays and collaborates with the Zionists will never find security."

Behind the words, a deeper rivalry
The exchange points to a deeper rift. The relations between the UAE, the first Gulf country to officially recognise Israel, and Saudi Arabia, which has refused to recognise Israel despite American pressure, have soured in the recent past largely over the latter’s support for Southern Yemeni separatist groups. 
Against this backdrop, the Mecca defence pact is being seen by analysts as a counter to the UAE-Israel military cooperation, which remains unpopular outside Israeli and American circles.
As Theodore Singer, a former US intelligence officer, told Middle East Eye, "At first glance, the UAE-Israel bloc delivers more tangible gains for both parties, but the Mecca pact may ultimately resonate more broadly and less transactionally.”
For example, when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that he visited the UAE at the height of the war on Iran, Abu Dhabi moved to deny the official statement.
In contrast, the Mecca pact was celebrated in public. It was announced that Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Turkish leader Recep Tayyip Erdogan joined together for Friday prayer in the holiest city in Islam.
Some analysts say that the very fact that Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have publicly codified their agreement gives it room to grow, potentially in ways the UAE-Israel alliance is unable to.
Saudi unease over Cairo’s UAE ‘subordination’
The same UAE-Saudi rivalry that appears to underpin Abdulla's remarks is also playing out over who has been left out of the pact. Saudi Arabia is learnt to have opposed Egypt’s entry into the new defence pact, citing growing unease over Cairo's "subordination" to the UAE as one of the reasons.
Sources had told MEE that while Egypt sent air defence systems and fighter jets to Abu Dhabi in response to Iranian attacks, and Sisi visited UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed more than once during the war, no such steps were taken towards Saudi Arabia. They concluded that Riyadh had become increasingly alarmed by Sisi's alignment with Abu Dhabi.
The sources said this was also due to Riyadh seeing several Emirati policies as running against Egypt's own strategic interests. These include the UAE’s involvement in Somaliland, its strategic relationship with Israel, its support for Ethiopia during disputes over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and its backing of the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan.

I wish I had been a more rebellious teenager, says Bella Ramsey
- Published
Bella Ramsey spent many teenage years working with adults so never really went through the moody, rebellious phase often associated with being a teenager.
The British actor, who debuted in Game of Thrones aged 11 and uses they/them pronouns, says they had consciously decided not to behave like a stereotypical teenager after hearing criticisms from adults.
"I was like, I'm not going to be that."
So when Sunny Dancer, a film about a summer camp for young people affected by cancer, gave Ramsey seven weeks to experience teenage freedom, it was an opportunity to dive straight in.
"I got to be a teenager aged 21, which was brilliant," Ramsey tells BBC News. "It was really nice - and liberating."
Looking back, Ramsey says the experience made them wonder whether they had missed out by being quite so sensible the first time around.
"I kind of wish that I had made the most of being a teenager and getting away with things and being a bit rebellious."
In Sunny Dancer, Ramsey plays Ivy, a young female cancer survivor in remission who reluctantly heads to a "chemo camp" where she finds an unexpected group of friends and has a summer that changes her.
The rest of the cast were more than happy to help fill in the gaps; Ramsey says younger co-stars discussed songs and nights out.
"They were teaching me what being a teenager was for them and I was learning all the songs like five years later."
An emotional moment at film's premiere
Beneath the summer camp fun is a story that is deeply personal for the film's writer and director, George Jaques.
His mother was diagnosed with cancer when he was 15, but it took another eight years for him to feel ready to turn some of those experiences into a script.
"I never seem to write in the moment I'm going through it," Jaques says. "You have to sort of get through and understand it and have that reflection of it."
He stresses that the film is not his family's story, but "there's bits of me" scattered throughout its characters.
Jaques was also conscious his own experience could only take him so far. So, he worked with the Teenage Cancer Trust, hearing from young cancer survivors as well as parents who had lost children.
"I remember going in to do a big talk with some young people who had survived cancer and they were like, 'don't call us kids, do not say we're brave.'"
He says the film was "shaped" by these young people he met - such that he gave two of them roles in it.
Making the movie also forced Jaques to revisit some of his own fears around loss. He recalls a moment during the premiere in Berlin when emotion crept up on him.
"I remember seeing my mother and I realised there's a version of that movie where my mum wasn't sitting in the audience," he says.
Both Ramsey and Jaques think we could be better at allowing people to experience grief without expecting them to quickly return to normal.
Jaques recalls losing someone close to him when he was 18, while sitting his A-levels.
"We are expected to just to carry on," he says, describing the instinct to go "straight back to work and school".
If we "really were honest with how we feel we might be able to understand it a bit better," he adds.
In the UK, there is no general legal right to paid bereavement leave when someone close to you dies. The main statutory exception is parental bereavement leave and pay following the death of a child under 18 or a stillbirth after 24 weeks.
Ramsey thinks there can be an instinct to minimise what you are going through.
"You speak to people who are grieving, you're like, 'How are you doing?' They're like, 'Oh, yeah, yeah, you know, it's hard, but I'm fine.' It feels very unhealthily British."
After spending seven weeks playing a teenager who is desperate to be their own person, Ramsey's advice for young people struggling to fit in is straightforward.
"Don't try and fit in. Please don't change to try and fit in because there are people who will fit in with you."
Jaques agrees, but says the responsibility should not all be placed on young people to become more resilient.
"There's so much pressure on young people to change on social media," he says. "Why don't we stop hating on young people? Maybe that's where we should start as well."

One of this summer’s biggest onscreen hits has had big beasts, great escapes and choppy waters, but it’s not Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey – it’s a livestream of Alaskan brown bears catching salmon.
The Brooks Falls bearcam at Katmai national park in the US was watched 7.3m times between 22 June and 4 August – up 70% from the same period last year and more than double the views it attracted in 2024.
The cameras, run by the wildlife network Explore.org, show brown bears gathering at Brooks Falls waterfall to catch sockeye salmon as they make their way upstream. More than a dozen bears at a time can be spotted prowling around the rocky waters and chomping on the fish.
Candice Rusch, Explore.org’s director of new media, said the surge in viewers appeared to be driven by the bears returning to the falls in large numbers after a less concentrated season last year.
“Last year was a really high salmon run, which meant there was salmon all over the river and the bears didn’t need to congregate at the falls the way they’re doing right now,” she said.
“This year we’ve just had very good views of large congregations of bears.
“It’s like the whole world discovered they could put bearcam on their TV at the same time,” she said. “Maybe people just have it on while they’re cooking dinner.”
The cameras were first installed in 2012 as part of an effort to bring remote wildlife into people’s homes. Rusch said the idea was that people were more likely to protect animals and landscapes they had come to know and care about.
Dr Jeffrey Skibins, an associate professor at East Carolina University, said: “Recent studies have shown that nature-based webcams are beneficial to both wildlife and people. They benefit wildlife by improving conservation attitudes, behaviours and awareness.
“This is not to suggest they are replacements for getting out in nature, but rather serve as viable additions,” he said.
The stream has developed a dedicated fanbase. Viewers can identify individual bears from features such as their ears, noses and body shape, and some keep detailed records of their feeding habits.
One dedicated fan reported watching a bear called Otis eat 42 salmon over several hours, which Rusch said could equate to more than 100,000 calories.
The bears’ gorging will take on added significance next month, when Katmai’s annual Fat Bear Week begins in the autumn. The public votes in a knockout-style competition to crown the park’s fattest bear, as the animals pile on winter weight in preparation for hibernation.
“The bears are great,” Rusch said. “This is an amazing place and it deserves all the love it’s getting.”

Nigeria's mass wedding - and how telling lovers from fraudsters is proving tricky
- Published
Celebrations have turned the northern Nigerian city of Kano into a riot of colour and excitement over the last week as 1,500 couples married at a mass wedding.
For days the city's streets have been buzzing with bridal parties and their families preparing outfits and attending other organised events.
On Friday, brides in red hijabs with grooms in matching red hats and white robes went to the palace of the Emir, the city's traditional Muslim leader, for the main ceremony where they officially became husband and wife.
The nuptials culminated on Saturday with a wedding breakfast hosted by Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, who offered his blessing to the newlyweds.
The Kano state government sponsored this initiative, spending 1.5bn naira ($1m; £815,000) to support those tying the knot - providing the bride's dowry and furniture for the couple's first home.
The scheme targets low-income individuals who cannot afford the significant financial costs associated with marriage.
The annual event was initiated in 2012 by the then-governor when 100 couples - primarily widows and divorcees - wed at the palace.
The mass weddings have continued under subsequent governors, with numbers expanding each year as demand has grown and included those in polygamous Muslim marriages.
Such is the popularity of the scheme that 5,000 couples applied this year.
The event is always overseen by the Hisbah - the city's Islamic police force - and one of their main tasks is to vet the couples wanting to wed.
Kano has a majority Muslim population and Sharia operates in the state alongside the secular legal system.
Mujahid Aminudeen, deputy commander-general of the Hisbah, admits it is not an easy task.
"Whenever we find out that there's something dubious or fishy about a couple, we disqualify them," he tells the BBC.
He says some couples will go to great lengths to convince the authorities that they are a genuine love match when their eye is more on the benefits on offer.
The state government has spent approximately 1m naira ($735; £544) on each participating couple.
According to the Hisbah, the support package a couple receives includes essential household items needed to establish a new home: beds, mattresses, bedsheets, pillows, furniture and food supplies.
Each bride receives a dowry of 100,000 naira, while a further 100,000 naira is provided as start-up capital to encourage small-scale entrepreneurship and help the couple achieve financial self-reliance after marriage.
All intending couples must undergo comprehensive medical examinations - including tests for HIV, hepatitis, pregnancy and genotype compatibility - before being cleared for the programme.
Aminudeen revealed that some couples had been disqualified after being discovered to have altered their medical test results.
In one case, an intending bride was found to have presented her brother as the groom in an attempt to benefit from the scheme.
Local journalist Yusuf Ali Abdallah, who has covered the mass weddings for years, said Nigeria's struggling economy had been fuelling desperation among the applicants this year.
"As we all know, marriage involves spending money and the country's economy is not bright at the moment," he told the BBC.
"This makes some people desperate to get on this list."
One couple who were already married had even attempted to present themselves as an intending pair before being detected and removed from the programme, he said.
Other charlatans have tried to take advantage of those desperate to get on the sponsored list, which was made public two weeks ago.
One Kano resident, who asked to be anonymous, said he had been asked to pay a bribe to get on the list.
"But to be fair to the organisers, I later found out those who asked me for money were not Hisbah staff," he said.
He and his fiancée failed to be chosen for this August's wedding but he said he would try again next year.
Aminudeen admitted that the Islamic police were aware of such allegations: "We have found that there are some people asking others to pay certain money so they can make the list."
But the Hisbah officer wanted to assure all those wishing to wed in future that the entire process should not cost them a single naira.
"We want to announce to the people of Kano that the whole process is free: from the selection to the medicals and the goods set aside for couples - all are covered by the government."
One of successful grooms, 43-year-old clothes trader Rabiu Yusuf, agreed the process of applying to be married had gone smoothly for him.
"Personally, no-one asked me for anything. I was told the government would sponsor it all," he told the BBC.
His new wife is Aisha Auwal - the couple met as she regularly visited his shop to buy clothes.
Yusuf, who already has five children with his first wife, said he was "very happy and can't wait to start a new life" with his customer-turned-bride.
24 year-old Amina Alhassan echoed his sentiments, adding that she had not encountered any problems when applying to marry 40-year-old Nura Abdullahi.
Their union was first arranged by their families in Dambatta village before they presented themselves to the Hisbah.
"Everything has been free and I want to commend the Kano government for this scheme because without it, many couldn't have afforded to marry due to the high cost of living."
After Saturday's wedding feast, the presentation of the household goods began.
But it will take several more days for the excitement to die down in Kano and as the newlyweds busy themselves with setting up home together.
